# XF Runtime Bridge MCP tool reference

Every tool the XF Runtime Bridge MCP server publishes: 160 tools, 89 of which change the game. The [MCP guide](mcp.md) explains installing the server, the safety model and a worked session; this page is generated from the command catalogue, so it always matches what the server lists.

Tool names are the catalogue's command names with dots as underscores (`photo.camera.set` is `photo_camera_set`). Every tool's description, parameters and refusals are written for the person using the AI client as much as for the model. A successful answer is JSON text with the `result`, an `undo` when the tool changed something, and a correlation id (`cid`) that matches the bridge's logs; captures also return a small preview image. A refusal is an error result with a plain sentence, the code in brackets and the correlation id.

## Permission classes

Each tool belongs to one class. The MCP server can withhold classes (`--read-only`, `--allow`), and the game's own gate in the bridge's `config.ini` is separate and final: without it every change is refused, whatever the MCP client allows.

| Class | Label | Tools | Changes the game | What it covers | Game-side switch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | Look | 59 | No | Reads what the game is doing, or takes a screenshot of its window. Changes nothing. | Always allowed while the bridge is on. |
| `notify` | Show messages in the game | 5 | No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel | Shows short messages to the player in the game (the ink panel while the HUD shows, the XF box (the small box with the yellow heading) in photo mode and menus, the CET line (one line with a coloured dot at the far top left) when neither can draw; none on a loading screen), and shows, hides or moves the ink panel. Changes nothing in the game; the messages fade by themselves. | Always allowed while the bridge is on, read-only builds included. |
| `write-photo` | Control photo mode | 16 | Yes | Opens and closes photo mode and changes its camera, lights, expression and on-screen menu. Nothing outlives photo mode. | `allow_writes = true` and `photo` in `allow_write_classes` (on by default once writes are allowed). |
| `write-world` | Change the world | 6 | Yes | Changes the in-game time of day or stops time, and places XF map pins (a test feature). Undo by setting it back or removing the pins. | `allow_writes = true` and `world` in `allow_write_classes` (on by default once writes are allowed). |
| `write-character` | Change V's appearance | 5 | Yes | Opens the appearance screen, changes its options and camera, and confirms or leaves it (opening and leaving only in the XF test profile). | `allow_writes = true` and `character` in `allow_write_classes` (on by default once writes are allowed); opening, confirming and leaving the appearance screen also need `allow_creator_leave = true`. |
| `write-inventory` | Change V's clothing | 5 | Yes | Equips and unequips V's clothing, and can add a test item to V's inventory (and remove it again). Off in the bridge's settings until the maintainer allows it; undo by equipping the earlier item. | `allow_writes = true` and `inventory` listed by name. Off in every package unless the test build is made with `--allow-inventory`. |
| `write-save` | Save and load the game | 6 | Yes | Makes a new manual save (never overwrites one) or loads a save, which discards everything since it. Saving is refused while the bridge's own changes are live unless explicitly overridden. | `allow_writes = true` and `save` listed by name (the test profile's build lists it). |
| `write-showroom` | Set up the finish showroom | 5 | Yes | Spawns XF Finish Showroom's mannequin heads and their light rigs in front of V, turns them and removes them again. Nothing is saved: clearing, the kill switch or loading a save removes them. Off in the bridge's settings except in the XF test profile. | `allow_writes = true` and `showroom` listed by name (the test profile's build lists it). |
| `write-player` | Move V | 8 | Yes | Moves and turns V (teleports with ground checks, glides along walkable paths), turns her view, crouches and stands, draws or holsters her weapon and opens menus. Reversible; the kill switch and loading a save undo it. Off in the bridge's settings except in the XF test profile. | `allow_writes = true` and `player` listed by name (the test profile's build lists it). |
| `write-npc` | Direct NPCs | 15 | Yes | Brings XF's own passers-by into the world near V and directs them and other NPCs close by: walking, following, lines of text and the game's own voice lines, where they look, their faces and gestures, and dialogue choices for V. Nothing is saved: releasing them, the kill switch or loading a save removes them, and saving waits until they are gone. Story characters, vendors, police and children are never touched. Off in the bridge's settings except in the XF test profile. | `allow_writes = true` and `npc` listed by name (the test profile's build lists it); spawning also needs Codeware and the -writes package's XF actor records (TweakXL). |
| `write-dm` | Direct the scene | 21 | Yes | Brings props, vehicles and lights into the world near V and changes doors and vehicles; plays sounds and a vehicle's radio; shows message toasts and a real incoming call from a contact the player has, with subtitle lines; puts an XF quest in the HUD's tracker; shows the game's own banners and quest toasts; and arms watchers that run micro-actions inside the game without the agent. Nothing is saved: the answers' undos, the kill switch, the pause, a handover or loading a save take it all back, and saving waits until the spawned things and changed doors are gone. Off in the bridge's settings except in the XF test profile. | `allow_writes = true` and `dm` listed by name (the test profile's build lists it); bringing things in and the subtitle lines also need Codeware, and the toolkit's scripts ship in the -writes package only. |
| `act-player` | Act for V | 2 | Yes | Irreversible actions in the world for V: using devices, choosing dialogue, consuming items. Reserved: no command uses it yet. Off in the bridge's settings except in the XF test profile. | `allow_writes = true` and `act` listed by name. Reserved: no tool uses it yet. |
| `control` | Stop the bridge | 7 | Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it | Switches the game bridge off until it is reconnected from inside the game (test builds) or the game restarts. Always allowed. | Always allowed; every MCP configuration includes it. |

## Refusals any tool can give

A refused tool changes nothing unless its message says otherwise (`timeout_after_start` is the one that may have happened), and its message is a plain sentence with one next step that a client can show as it is. The codes below can come from many tools, so each tool's own list ("Refusals") shows the codes the catalogue declares for it and those its description and parameters mention; it is not exhaustive.

- **Any tool:** [`bad_input`](#refusal-bad-input).
- **Any tool that reaches the game** (everything except `capture_screenshot` and `capture_recrop`, which work on the game window without the bridge): [`no_bridge`](#refusal-no-bridge), [`bridge_busy`](#refusal-bridge-busy), [`session_running`](#refusal-session-running), [`wrong_server`](#refusal-wrong-server), [`access_denied`](#refusal-access-denied), [`connect_failed`](#refusal-connect-failed), [`disconnected`](#refusal-disconnected), [`client_timeout`](#refusal-client-timeout), [`game_not_running`](#refusal-game-not-running), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout), [`timeout_after_start`](#refusal-timeout-after-start), [`busy`](#refusal-busy), [`rate_limited`](#refusal-rate-limited), [`killed`](#refusal-killed), [`script_calls_unavailable`](#refusal-script-calls-unavailable), [`script_layer_missing`](#refusal-script-layer-missing), [`unknown_method`](#refusal-unknown-method), [`rtti_missing`](#refusal-rtti-missing), [`rtti_signature`](#refusal-rtti-signature), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`failed`](#refusal-failed).
- **Any tool that changes the game:** [`writes_disabled`](#refusal-writes-disabled), [`write_class_disabled`](#refusal-write-class-disabled), [`writes_paused`](#refusal-writes-paused), [`handed_over`](#refusal-handed-over), [`bad_params`](#refusal-bad-params).

Each class's tools also refuse at moments that class cares about:

- **`write-photo`:** [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), [`write_mismatch`](#refusal-write-mismatch).
- **`write-world`:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay).
- **`write-character`:** [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu), [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v).
- **`write-inventory`:** [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`not_added_by_bridge`](#refusal-not-added-by-bridge), [`no_active_outfit`](#refusal-no-active-outfit), [`outfit_managed_elsewhere`](#refusal-outfit-managed-elsewhere), [`script_outfit_api_changed`](#refusal-script-outfit-api-changed).
- **`write-save`:** [`bridge_save_lock`](#refusal-bridge-save-lock), [`bridge_effects_active`](#refusal-bridge-effects-active), [`saving_locked`](#refusal-saving-locked), [`no_free_slot`](#refusal-no-free-slot), [`save_failed`](#refusal-save-failed), [`save_uncertain`](#refusal-save-uncertain), [`save_not_found`](#refusal-save-not-found).

## Connection, session and answers

Check the connection, read the game's phase, follow the session's event stream, ask the player a question in the game and wait for the answer, hand the game over to the player and take it back.

### `bridge_ping`

**Check the game connection.** Checks that the game is running with XF Runtime Bridge and answering. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `bridge.ping`, the bridge method `ping`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `bridge_info`

**Bridge details.** Shows the bridge and game versions, whether changes are allowed (allow_writes), and connection counts.

- **Command:** `bridge.info`, the bridge method `bridge.info`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `bridge_kill`

**Switch the bridge off.** Emergency stop: switches the game bridge off and puts back what it left switched on (a frozen world, a hidden photo-mode menu, a live-posed carrier). Nothing can reach the game through it afterwards, until the player presses Reconnect in the game's XF Runtime Bridge window (Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay, test builds) or restarts the game. The game itself keeps running.

- **Command:** `bridge.kill`, the bridge method `bridge.kill`
- **Permission:** Stop the bridge (`control`)
- **Changes the game:** Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it
- **Undo:** In the game, press Reconnect in the XF Runtime Bridge window (Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay; test builds), or restart the game.

No parameters.

### `session_events`

**Read the session's event stream.** What happened in the game session, in order, from the bridge's own record: every write it answered (with its undo) or refused, the kill switch, handovers and resumes, behaviours starting, progressing and stopping (with why and what they gave back), and notes (from session_note or a button in the game). Successful writer world.probe, scene.read and world.district calls also publish observe.result with command, cid, writer connection generation and result, without another game read. The complete serialized event is capped at 8192 bytes; truncated true keeps a structured leading result prefix (JSON object key order), with the provenance fields retained. Reader calls do not republish. Give since (the next value of the last read) to read only what came after.

- **Command:** `session.events`, the bridge method `session.events`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | integer | at least 0 | Only events after this sequence number (default 0: the oldest kept). |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 500 | At most this many events, 1 to 500. Default 100. |
| `kinds` | array of string | at most 16 items; each at most 32 characters | Only these kinds (write, refused, kill, handover, resume, behaviour, note, observe.result; 0.8.6: ink_tree, ink_pointer, ink_input from the panel inside photo mode's menu). |

### `session_log`

**Read or follow the session log.** The session's log in one list: the bridge's event stream and the tools' own record of commands (and notes), merged by time; the last tail entries (default 50). follow_ms waits up to that long for something new from the game, for tailing.

- **Command:** `session.log`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tail` | integer | 1 to 500 | How many entries, 1 to 500. Default 50. |
| `since` | integer | at least 0 | Bridge events after this sequence number (a previous answer's next). |
| `kinds` | array of string | at most 16 items; each at most 32 characters | Only these kinds. |
| `sources` | array of string | at most 2 items; each `bridge`, `tools` | bridge, tools, or both (default). |
| `follow_ms` | integer | 0 to 30000 | Wait up to this long for new bridge events, 0 to 30000 ms. Default 0. |

### `session_note`

**Add a note to the session log.** Adds a line to the session's event stream (and the tools' own log), for a finding, a question or a marker between steps; show also puts it on screen under the in-game label for 10 s. Changes nothing in the game.

- **Command:** `session.note`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Show messages in the game (`notify`)
- **Changes the game:** No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel
- **Undo:** A note stays in the log; it changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` (required) | string | 1 to 500 characters | The note, one line. |
| `level` | string | `info`, `warn`, `ask`, `done` | info (default), warn, ask or done. |
| `show` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Also show it on screen under the in-game label (default false). |

### `session_handover`

**Hand the game to the player.** Gives the game to the player in one step: stops every behaviour, shows photo mode's menu and cursor again if the bridge hid them, clears the showroom's light rigs if lights is clear (so the player lights the heads with photo mode's own lights), then pauses the bridge and gives V back as player_stop does (every effect the bridge put on her, such as a crouch or a glide's movement hold, lifted; any look it started ended) and releases every NPC it directs (actors removed, dialogue choices and lines taken down): every change it is asked for is refused until session_resume. A line in the game says so, and the session log records it. Reads, notes and the kill switch still work.

- **Command:** `session.handover`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Stop the bridge (`control`)
- **Changes the game:** Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it
- **Undo:** session_resume gives the bridge its changes back.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lights` | string | `keep`, `clear` | keep (default) or clear the showroom's rigs. |
| `restore_ui` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Show photo mode's menu and cursor again (default true). |
| `note` | string | at most 200 characters | Why, for the log (for example what the player should judge). |
| `quiet` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Post no notice in the game (a script's own brief pause); an earlier notice is still withdrawn. |

### `session_resume`

**Take the game back from the player.** Ends a handover: the bridge may change the game again (within what its settings allow). A line in the game says so, and the session log records it.

- **Command:** `session.resume`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Stop the bridge (`control`)
- **Changes the game:** Only the bridge's own work: it stops or pauses it
- **Undo:** session_handover hands over again.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | string | at most 200 characters | What the player did or decided, for the log. |
| `quiet` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Post no line in the game (a script's own brief pause); the handover notice is still withdrawn. |

### `game_status`

**What the game is doing.** Says what the game is doing right now (phase: starting, main_menu, loading, gameplay, photo_mode, character_menu, menu or paused), the game version, whether V is in the world, whether photo mode is open or allowed, whether saving is locked, and whether changes are allowed at all (allow_writes).

- **Command:** `game.status`, the bridge method `game.status`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `game_wait`

**Wait for a game phase.** Waits until the game reaches one of the given phases (for example photo_mode after asking the player to open it, or character_menu at a mirror), checking twice a second. Use it between steps that depend on something the player does.

- **Command:** `game.wait`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** `wait_timeout`, `interrupted`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phase` (required) | string or array of string | `starting`, `main_menu`, `loading`, `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `character_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `shutting_down`; or 1 to 9 items; each `starting`, `main_menu`, `loading`, `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `character_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `shutting_down` | The phase to wait for, or a list of phases (any one of them). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | 0 to 600000 | How long to wait, in milliseconds (default 60000, at most 600000). |

### `game_options_read`

**Graphics and render settings.** Reads the settings that change how V looks in a screenshot, without changing any: the upscaler and its mode (DLAA among them), frame generation, ray and path tracing, subsurface-scattering quality, HDR and the camera effects (film grain, chromatic aberration, depth of field, lens flares, motion blur, vignette), as a short summary plus every setting of those graphics and display groups. With Cyber Engine Tweaks loaded it also reads the game's hidden character render options (hair, skin, rim light and eyes; for example what a rendering preset mod changed), or names given in names.

- **Command:** `game.options.read`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Read the graphics and display settings. Default true. |
| `render_options` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Read the hidden character render options through Cyber Engine Tweaks. Default true. |
| `groups` | array of string | 1 to 6 items; each `/graphics/presets`, `/graphics/advanced`, `/graphics/raytracing`, `/graphics/basic`, `/graphics/performance`, `/video/display` | Only these settings groups (default all of them). |
| `names` | array of string | 1 to 128 items; each at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | Render options to read instead of the default character set, as Category/Name (for example Editor/Characters/Hair/GlobalLight/R). |

### `ui_message`

**Show a message in the game.** Shows a message to the player in the game, so the player never has to leave it: on the one status surface showing (0.8.2: the ink panel while the game shows its HUD, the XF box with the yellow heading in photo mode and menus, the CET line with a coloured dot at the far top left only when neither can draw; 0.8.3: none on a loading screen), and a question also in the XF Runtime Bridge window of the Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay. Up to 600 characters, wrapped, for seconds seconds (default 8); a longer text is cut at a word with an ellipsis. At most four show at once; a new one pushes out the oldest, except the newest unanswered question, which stays pinned until it is answered or its seconds end. level colours it: info, ask (a question for the player), warn or done. A question (level ask) shows only the answers choices gives (1 to 4 short labels, such as Fully visible and Partly cut off, or Yes and No); without choices it shows one Done button, for a step the player confirms. The player answers with the key shown next to each answer (F6, F7, F8, F11 by default) or the button in the XF Runtime Bridge window, and the answer (with this message's id) goes into the session's event stream, where session_wait returns it; the question stays with Answered: and the answer until the next message. Characters a surface can't draw show as one replacement mark there, and Cyber Engine Tweaks' label writes Polish and other Latin letters without their accents. One question at a time: a new question withdraws one still waiting (its session_wait ends with question_gone). Each answer in choices is a button label of at most 24 characters; put any detail in the question's text. clear: true takes the lines down and withdraws a question still waiting (keep_asks: true keeps it); withdraw takes one message down by its id (a question's undo). The kill switch clears them all.

- **Command:** `ui.message`, the bridge method `ui.message`
- **Permission:** Show messages in the game (`notify`)
- **Changes the game:** No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel
- **Undo:** The result's undo withdraws the message by its id; messages also fade by themselves.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | 1 to 2000 characters | The message (at most 600 characters are shown). |
| `seconds` | integer | 1 to 600 | How long it shows, 1 to 600 seconds. Default 8; give a question long enough for the player to answer. |
| `level` | string | `info`, `ask`, `warn`, `done` | info (default), ask, warn or done. |
| `choices` | array of string | 1 to 4 items; each 1 to 24 characters | With level ask: the answers offered, only these, 1 to 4 button labels of at most 24 characters each (default one Done button). |
| `clear` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Remove the lines first (alone: only that), and withdraw a question still waiting for its answer (a session_wait on it ends with question_gone). |
| `keep_asks` | boolean | `true`, `false` | With clear: keep a question still waiting for its answer (a capture's clear does). |
| `withdraw` | integer | 1 to 1000000000 | Take down the message with this id (ui_message's id); a question withdrawn this way ends its session_wait with question_gone. |

### `input_probe`

**Probe the game's test input system.** Read-only research for input without window focus: whether the game has CD PROJEKT RED's functional-test system and its fake-input functions (their parameter counts and, for offline disassembly, where their code is in the executable), the related player, navigation and UI test functions, whether that system exists in the game now, whether the game window is in front, and which module the game's pad-input import resolves to. Calls none of them.

- **Command:** `input.probe`, the bridge method `input.probe`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `session_wait`

**Wait for the player's answer.** Waits until the player answers a question from the game or sends a comment (or another event kind you name), then returns it: kinds (default answer and comment; note catches notes from the game, such as Mark this moment, never a client's own), message_id (only the answer to that ui_message question counts, even one given before this call; other kinds still end the wait from now on; a question withdrawn, cleared or run out of time without an answer ends it with question_gone), after (the event sequence to wait after; default: now) and timeout_s (1 to 600, default 120). Answers come from the answer keys or the buttons in the XF Runtime Bridge window of the Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay; comments from that window's comment box. Use it after ui_message with level ask instead of polling session_log. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `session.wait`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** `question_gone`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | array of string | 1 to 53 items; each `answer`, `comment`, `note`, `behaviour`, `kill`, `handover`, `resume`, `write`, `refused`, `save`, `input.submitted`, `input.result`, `input.photo.callback`, `input.photo.hide`, `input.photo.confirmation`, `input.ui.consumed`, `input.ui.queued`, `input.ui.dequeued`, `input.ui.native`, `choice.offer`, `choice.selection`, `choice.attempt`, `choice.result`, `npc.spawned`, `npc.arrived`, `npc.blocked`, `npc.move_failed`, `npc.follow_ended`, `npc.turned`, `npc.said`, `npc.act_done`, `npc.choice`, `npc.released`, `npc.dissolved`, `npc.handed_back`, `npc.lost`, `npc.died`, `npc.auto_released`, `npc.substitute_started`, `npc.substituted`, `npc.substitute_failed`, `npc.restored`, `npc.original_returned`, `npc.original_unreturned`, `dm.watch`, `dm.micro`, `dm.phone`, `dm.quest`, `dm.world`, `dm.audio`, `dm.light`, `dm.notify`, `dm.released` | Event kinds that end the wait (default answer and comment). |
| `message_id` | integer | 1 to 1000000000 | Only the answer to this question (ui_message's id) ends the wait, even one given before the call; other kinds still count. |
| `after` | integer | 0 to 1000000000000 | Wait for events after this sequence number (session_events' next); default: the newest when the call starts. |
| `timeout_s` | number | 1 to 600 | Give up after this many seconds, 1 to 600. Default 120. |
| `poll_ms` | integer | 200 to 2000 | How often the stream is read, 200 to 2000 ms. Default 400. |

## Photo mode

Open and leave photo mode, frame V, set the camera, lights, expression, pose and scene rows, and hide the menu for a clean capture. Nothing outlives photo mode.

### `photo_state`

**Photo mode state.** Whether photo mode is open or allowed, and (with menu) every photo-mode menu item the game set up: its number, label, range or options and current value. options adds each option list (for example every expression with its menu value, data, and its face table index, table_index, with table_index_by saying whether it was matched by the expression's name or, less surely, by its position; the expression item's face_table says how many of photo mode's expression records were listed and could be read, so an option without table_index is explained).

- **Command:** `photo.state`, the bridge method `photo.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menu` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Include the menu items. |
| `options` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Include every option list (implies menu). |

### `photo_open`

**Open photo mode.** Opens photo mode by pressing the player's own photo mode key in the game window (read from the game's key bindings, N by default): the only key the XF tools ever send, and only to the game window. It checks first that V is in the world and the game allows photo mode, and by default sends only while the game window is already in front: otherwise it refuses (not_foreground) without touching any window, since bringing the game forward catches whatever the player is typing elsewhere. focus: bring_to_front brings it forward first (the old behaviour). Then it waits until photo mode is open. The game has no in-engine way to open the full photo mode that is known to be safe (see the knowledge base), so the key stays the route. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `photo.open`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Control photo mode (`write-photo`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** photo.exit.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), `photo_not_allowed`, `key_unsupported`, `no_window`, `photo_open_timeout`, `interrupted`, [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| `focus` | string | `require`, `bring_to_front` | sendinput only: require (default: send only while the game window is already in front, else refuse and touch nothing) or bring_to_front (bring the game window forward first; anything the player is typing elsewhere goes to the game). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | 500 to 30000 | How long to wait for photo mode after the key, in milliseconds (default 5000). |

**Frame the photo-mode shot.** Sets the photo-mode camera: a named preset (face: V's face filling most of the frame, facing the camera. ### `photo_camera_place`

**Place the photo-mode camera (research).** Research (0.5.2): moves photo mode's own camera to a place and aims it, instead of moving V in front of it (photo mode's menu only moves V: up_down, near_far and left_right). Target: look_at (a world point), target v (V's eyes) or piece (a showroom head's eyes, for framing the finish showroom). Where: position (a world point), or distance_m from the target (default 1.5) at azimuth_deg (from the way the target faces, counter-clockwise seen from above: 0 in front, 90 its left) and elevation_deg. The camera's entity is moved with the teleportation facility, then the active camera is read a few frames later: held says whether photo mode kept it there (session 6's question; if not, photo mode places its camera itself and nothing is left to undo). Within 30 m of V, in photo mode only. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. ### `photo_expression_index`

**Apply a photo-mode face index (research).** Research tool for the expression editor: applies a photo-mode face table index (photo_state options' table_index, not the menu value) to V directly, the way photo mode feeds its face animation, without going through the expression list. It acts on V's photo-mode stand-in, where session 4 found the face rig; target head (the head item) is refused, since it has no face rig and the index changed nothing there. Whether the face changed shows only in a screenshot. By default only a table index of the expression list is accepted, and only one photo_state found by the expression's name (table_index_verified); one known only by list position (table_index_by position, which session 4 showed isn't the table index with an expression pack) is refused (unverified_index) unless force: true. unlisted: true allows any index (sparse-index checks). The answer's index_by says how the index was checked. Photo mode only, in the XF test profile. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

### `pose_live_read`

**Check the live-pose carrier in memory (research).** Research tool for live posing: finds a loaded animation clip in the game's memory (by default the XF live carrier from the test package, while photo mode shows it) and checks that its keys are laid out as the bridge expects: counts, key runs, joint indices and the carrier contract (one constant rotation key per joint). If anything differs it stops and lists every mismatch; otherwise it returns the decoded keys and a hash to compare with the Studio's offline decode (expect_hash). Changes nothing.

- **Permission:** Look (`read`)

### `pose_live_apply`

**Pose V live through the carrier (research).** Research tool for live posing: writes joint rotations (unit quaternions [x, y, z, w], by joint name or index) and optionally the Hips translation into the XF live carrier clip in the game's memory, so the photo-mode pose changes without a reload if the engine reads those keys every frame (the experiment's question). Only in the XF test profile's -writes build (allow_live_pose), in photo mode with the carrier selected (photo_pose_set record xfs_live_carrier), and only after the same layout checks as pose_live_read. restore: true puts the carrier's own keys back. ### `photo_subject`

**Where V and the camera are.** Reads where V's head is in the world and on screen (plus an optional point relative to it: up, forward and right in metres), the photo-mode camera's position, directions, field of view and aspect ratio, and V's current placement values. photo_frame uses it; it changes nothing.

- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

| `up` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres above V's head joint (world vertical). |

| `right` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres to V's right of the head joint. |

### `photo_frame`

**Frame V automatically.** Frames V in photo mode without hand-tuned values: turns V to face the camera (plus yaw_offset degrees for a light sweep), puts the target (eyes: Both eyes and brows, filling the eyes region (the window's centre band).; face: The face from chin to hairline, filling the face region.; head-and-shoulders: Head and shoulders.; full-body: V from head to feet, standing.) at the centre of the window (or at position) and sets the field of view so span_m metres fill the window height. Each frame starts from its lens's known pose (face and eyes: a portrait lens from about 2 m, so repeated frames never drift) and stays within the lens's limits, or is refused. Any refusal or failure part-way puts back everything it changed whose earlier value the game reported (the field of view, V's placement, and the camera preset, roll and look-at it set), names anything it couldn't, and carries the undo in its detail. It measures where V is through the game's camera (or, if that isn't available, from window captures, more roughly) and corrects in a few steps; converged also needs V to face the requested direction within 3 degrees (residual.facing_deg). The result records the lens, the camera's distance, the chosen values and an undo. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `photo.frame`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Control photo mode (`write-photo`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo puts the field of view, V's rotation and placement (and look-at, roll and camera preset) back as they were.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), `framing_bound`, `no_projection`, `no_response`, `no_capture`, `not_found`, [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`write_mismatch`](#refusal-write-mismatch), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | `eyes`, `face`, `head-and-shoulders`, `full-body` | What to frame. Default face. |
| `span_m` | number | 0.02 to 5 | World height in metres that fills the window height (default: 0.2 eyes, 0.36 face, 0.8 head-and-shoulders, 2 full-body). |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | The target point relative to V's head joint, in metres (overrides the framing's own). |
| `offset.up` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres up. |
| `offset.forward` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres forward (V's facing). |
| `offset.right` | number | -2 to 2 | Metres to V's right. |
| `position` | object | the fields below | Where the target should sit, as fractions of the window (default the centre). |
| `position.x` | number | 0 to 1 | 0 left edge, 1 right edge. |
| `position.y` | number | 0 to 1 | 0 top edge, 1 bottom edge. |
| `xf_preset` | boolean | `true`, `false` | First select the framing's XF camera preset (6 full body, 7 face, 8 eyes, 9 head and shoulders; needs the test profile's preset file), then fine-tune. |
| `camera_preset` | integer | 0 to 9 | First select this photo-mode camera preset (0-9), then fine-tune. |
| `keep_roll` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Keep the camera preset's own roll. Default false: the camera is levelled (roll 0) after selecting a preset. |
| `reseat_camera` | boolean | `true`, `false` | 0.7: when photo mode's camera is more than 4 m from V (a drone camera flown off) and the lens isn't keep, first select camera preset 1 to bring it back near V. Default true. |
| `face_camera` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Turn V to face the camera first. Default true. |
| `yaw_offset` | number | -180 to 180 | Degrees V turns away from facing the camera (counter-clockwise seen from above), for light sweeps and profile checks: 90 shows V's right side, 180 the back of V's head. Photo Mode Ex keeps V's rotation within -180 to 180. |
| `lens` | string | `portrait`, `wide`, `keep` | Where the frame starts and the limits it keeps: portrait: A long lens from about 2 m: natural facial proportions (the default for face and eyes).; wide: A wide lens from about 30 cm (the old face framing): exaggerated perspective, for comparison.; keep: Start from the current camera and placement (the default for head-and-shoulders, full-body and after a camera preset).. Default: portrait for face and eyes, keep for the others and after a camera preset. A frame that would need to leave its lens's limits is refused (framing_bound) with the camera put back. |
| `look_at` | string | `keep`, `off`, `camera` | V's look-at before framing: keep (default), off (V's head follows the body, for light sweeps) or camera. |
| `method` | string | `auto`, `project`, `capture` | auto (default: the game's camera, else window captures), project (the game's camera only) or capture (window captures only). |
| `max_steps` | integer | 1 to 12 | Most correction steps (default 6). |
| `tolerance` | number | 0.001 to 0.2 | Allowed centring error as a fraction of the window height (default 0.01). |
| `when` | object | the fields below | Conditions compared on each executing game frame |
| `when.phase` | string | `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `main_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `character_menu` | Required phase |
| `when.vehicle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be mounted/unmounted |
| `when.combat` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be in/out of combat |
| `when.photo_mode` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Photo mode must be active/inactive |
| `when.spawned` | array of integer | 1 to 16 items; each 1 to 2147483647 | Returned spawn handles that must still resolve |

## Appearance screen (character creator)

Read V's creator options, open the appearance screen from normal play, change options through their own rows, and confirm or back out.

### `player_appearance`

**V's appearance settings.** Reads V's character-creator state: body and voice, life path and hair-length tags. While the appearance screen (a mirror) is open it also lists every option with its current value; give option to see one option's full list of values. Outside the screen the game's option list isn't live, so only those flags are: the answer adds last_creator_reading, the last full list read on the screen this game session with its age in seconds (not live: a Back after it discarded its changes), when there is one. check asks whether V's finalized look has particular options (group and option names).

- **Command:** `player.appearance`, the bridge method `player.appearance`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | string | at most 128 characters | One option's internal name or on-screen label (appearance screen only). |
| `check` | array of object | at most 16 items | Options to look for in V's finalized look. |
| `check[].group` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | Customization group name. |
| `check[].option` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | Option name. |
| `check[].fpp` | boolean | `true`, `false` | First-person variant. |

### `cc_open`

**Open the appearance screen.** Opens the appearance screen (the mirror's character creator) from normal play, the way a mirror does, and waits until it is open. mode mirror (the default) allows the rows a mirror allows (hair, make-up, eye colour, piercings and the XF rows); ripperdoc also allows the face-shape, skin and cyberware rows. edit_mode new_game opens it in the new-game edit mode instead, as Character Customization Anywhere's F12 did in session 4: every row can change, the world isn't frozen, and Confirm still keeps the look; which edit mode avoids the stuck, half-open creator is a session 5 question. If the wait runs out, the request is withdrawn and the pause menu may open instead (Esc closes it). Refused in combat, a scene, a vehicle or a menu, when the player isn't V (a Johnny section), and until the game has registered the bridge's own save lock (it locks saving itself, until a save is loaded). If the wait runs out after the game took the request, the answer says the screen may still open (check game_status). Only in the XF test profile.

- **Command:** `cc.open`, the bridge method `cc.open`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.back (or Back in the appearance screen) discards every change made there and closes it.
- **Refusals:** [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`save_lock_not_held`](#refusal-save-lock-not-held), [`creator_open_timeout`](#refusal-creator-open-timeout), [`creator_open_uncertain`](#refusal-creator-open-uncertain), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `mirror`, `ripperdoc` | Which rows can be changed: mirror (default) or ripperdoc (adds the eye shape, nose, skin and cyberware rows). |
| `edit_mode` | string | `edit_tag`, `new_game` | The creator's edit mode: edit_tag (default: the mode's own tag, HairDresser or Ripperdoc, which freezes the world while the screen is open) or new_game (the NewGame tag Character Customization Anywhere's F12 ran with in session 4: every row editable, no freeze; not with mode ripperdoc). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | 500 to 15000 | How long to wait for the screen, in milliseconds (default 5000). |

### `cc_apply`

**Change one appearance option.** While the appearance screen is open (at a mirror or ripperdoc), sets one character-creator option to a value, exactly as clicking it does. option is the option's internal name, its on-screen label (for example XF) or its slot (for example piercings_color or makeupLips_color, the colour row of whichever style is chosen: a colour row named by its own name, such as makeupLips_08, belongs to one style and is refused unless that style is chosen). Give index (counting from 0), value (a value's internal name or on-screen label, where 5 and 05 are the same position; a word such as gold also finds the one value whose name contains it) or label (the name the creator shows, matched loosely: case, spaces and punctuation don't matter, and every word given must appear, so Grace Bob V4 finds Grace - Side Swept Bob - V4); the answer gives the index chosen. It never confirms: the player keeps the look by confirming, or backs out to discard every change. Refused anywhere else.

- **Command:** `cc.apply`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.apply with the previous index (in the result's undo), or Back in the appearance screen, which discards every change made there.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu), [`stale_match`](#refusal-stale-match), [`busy`](#refusal-busy)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The option's internal name, on-screen label or slot. |
| `index` | integer | 0 to 100000 | The value, counting from 0. |
| `value` | string | at most 128 characters | The value's internal name or on-screen label, instead of index. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 128 characters | The value's name as the creator shows it, matched loosely (see above), instead of index. |
| `expect_option` | string | 1 to 128 characters | With index: the option row read before (player_appearance's option name); refused (stale_match) if option now resolves to another row. label does this itself. |
| `expect_value` | string | 1 to 256 characters | With index: the value's internal name read before at that index; refused (stale_match) if it has another name now. label does this itself. |

### `cc_page`

**Point the appearance screen's camera.** Moves the open appearance screen's camera to one part of V, as hovering over a row does: skin, hair, eyes, teeth, nose, lips, jaw, head, nails, body, or default (where the screen started). Changing an option through cc_apply already moves it to that option's part; this is for looking without changing anything.

- **Command:** `cc.page`, the bridge method `cc.page`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** cc.page with page default (the camera's earlier part can't be read).
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` (required) | string | `skin`, `hair`, `eyes`, `teeth`, `nose`, `lips`, `jaw`, `head`, `nails`, `body`, `default` | The part of V to look at. |

### `cc_confirm`

**Confirm the appearance screen.** Presses Confirm on the open appearance screen (mirror or ripperdoc), keeping the look in the running game and closing the screen. Only in the XF test profile, and only in sessions that end by loading the safety save; saving stays locked while the change is live. Refused on a creator opened in new-game mode, where Confirm wouldn't keep the look.

- **Command:** `cc.confirm`, the bridge method `cc.confirm`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Load the safety save (the look stays in the running game until then).
- **Refusals:** [`creator_leave_disabled`](#refusal-creator-leave-disabled), [`not_in_character_menu`](#refusal-not-in-character-menu), [`busy`](#refusal-busy)

No parameters.

### `cc_back`

**Leave the appearance screen without keeping changes.** Presses Back on the open appearance screen and confirms it, discarding every change made there and closing the screen. It works even while the screen still seems busy with a change (a completion that never came): Back discards that change too, and the answer says busy_cleared. Only in the XF test profile.

- **Command:** `cc.back`, the bridge method `cc.back`
- **Permission:** Change V's appearance (`write-character`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Nothing to undo: the changes made on the screen were discarded.

## Test source recorder

Explicit autonomous -writes candidate only. Bounded source sampling and private chunks; not rendered or audible proof.

### `recorder_status`

**Observe source recorder.** Autonomous -writes test build and allow_test_hooks only. Find the current or last recorder run, including from a reader connection. Returns active, run, session (current bridge session), world (the run's generation), channels, start {s, at, uncertainty_ms}, latest (newest record sequence), stop_reason, requested_hz, duration_s, byte_cap and ack (the writer's last acknowledged sequence). start.s uses the recorder's QPC seconds; start.at is UTC ISO time with milliseconds, calibrated once at start and kept identical to the manifest start_at/start_sync; uncertainty_ms is the elapsed QPC interval bracketing the UTC read, separate from timestamp precision and OS accuracy. Before any run, active is false, channels is empty and all run-specific fields are unset. While active, stop_reason is unset; afterwards it is the last run's reason. Answered from a locked state copy on the bridge thread: no game-thread call, lease, acknowledgement or recorder change. Use a returned positive run for the first game.catchup call; the observer may poll every five seconds while visible.

- **Command:** `recorder.status`, the bridge method `recorder.status`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

No parameters.

### `test_record_start`

**Start source recording.** Autonomous -writes test build and allow_test_hooks only. One bounded owner samples fresh V, selected actors and camera on 100 ms game-update deadlines. Default channels include supervisor interventions and contacts: V car-hit entry plus landing/wall controller reports (ground included, other identity unknown), with partial uncommissioned coverage; absence is never full no-contact proof. Optional face (F) submissions and ui (U) consumer snapshots observe intent and actual widget state, never evaluated facial output. Optional incidents (0.8.20) records each witness.report (an incident V saw or heard, with its people, place, time and perception) as it closes, plus a one-second coverage heartbeat of the incident counters; passive, never a default channel. Optional events (0.8.25) copies each retained world.events envelope at ingress, plus a coverage heartbeat; no polling, no default channel. Optional subtitles and voice channels record callback events with 1 Hz coverage heartbeats; voice means covered script requests, never audibility. Reports achieved cadence, missed deadlines, QPC source times, age and drops; never resamples the NPC cache. V carries game_time_s (total TimeSystem seconds, unavailable if the clock cannot be read). First samples emit actor.identity records with entity, character record, affiliation, crowd and the record display-name key, once per entity per run/world, capped at 2048; actor_identity_omitted counts attempts beyond the cap. Manifest start_at/start_sync and each chunk sync map QPC to UTC, with uncertainty_ms. Stop and drain before another start.

- **Command:** `test.record.start`, the bridge method `test.record.start`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`recording_busy`](#refusal-recording-busy), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

## Player

Read V's state, move and turn her, turn her view, crouch, draw or holster, open menus, and give her back.

### `player_state`

**Read V's state.** V in the world: position (her feet: the entity's origin on the ground; 0.8.4, session 11's L5), facing (yaw), the camera's place (camera.position: in first person her eyes, about 1.6 m above position), direction, yaw and pitch, the player state machine (locomotion, high level, scene tier, vehicle, combat), whether she is in combat, a vehicle, a scene or a dialogue, why the bridge wouldn't move her now (busy), what she is looking at (with whether it is an interaction target), the effects the bridge put on her and the behaviours running.

- **Command:** `player.state`, the bridge method `player.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay)

No parameters.

### `player_teleport`

**Teleport V.** Moves V to a world point (position) or an offset from her (forward, right, up along her facing), and/or turns her (yaw absolute, turn relative), through the game's own teleport. By default the point snaps to walkable ground within 2 m and is refused where there is none (no_ground); ground exact skips the snap at your own risk. Either way a point more than 0.5 m away is refused where the world isn't loaded (not_streamed). At most 50 m unless far; at most two teleports a second. The answer reads her place back two ticks later (settled); teleport does not apply a movement hold (held: false). Refuses only a positive Road classification unless allow_road:true; positive CrossWalk is allowed with a traffic caution. Unknown containment proceeds with traffic_risk unknown and a plain warning in the answer and catch-up; the override is not needed for unknown. The current reader returns unknown everywhere, with no fabricated pavement suggestion. A turn in place remains exact. Existing behaviours must be stopped first. Positions here (position, before, now and the undo's) are her feet, as player_state's position, never the camera's: an undo with ground exact puts her feet back exactly where they were. It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which). Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `player.teleport`, the bridge method `player.teleport`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo teleports V back to where she stood, facing the same way; loading the save undoes it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`no_ground`](#refusal-no-ground), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

### `player_look`

**Turn V's view.** Turns V's view to yaw and pitch (degrees; relative adds them to the current view) or towards a world point (at): instant (her facing by a teleport in place, the pitch by a very short look-at) or smooth over duration_s (along the shortest arc, eased in and out, in short steps of the game's own look-at, so it takes duration_s; the player's mouse or stick ends it, took_over camera_drift). Answers the angles reached, whether they are within 2 degrees, took_s and whether player_stop stopped it. Normal play only. It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which). Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `player.look`, the bridge method `player.look`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo turns the view back to the earlier angles.

### `player_action`

**Do a system-driven action.** One of the actions the game's systems can do without input: crouch and stand (the game's own forced crouch, as a sniper nest uses it; only the bridge's own is lifted), weapon.draw, weapon.arms (0.7: the arm cyberware's weapon, such as Mantis Blades, drawn), weapon.holster and weapon.slot (1-3) through the equipment system's own requests, menu.open (inventory, map, journal, perks, crafting, or the wardrobe screen) and menu.close. Jumping, sprinting and dodging need an input channel (research). It checks V first and refuses with the reason (in_combat, in_vehicle, in_scene, player_busy while she jumps, slides, falls or lands, swims, sits in a workspot, takes someone down or carries a body, or a menu or photo mode is open; player_state's busy_state says which). ### `player_status`

**Read V's status.** V's life state in one read: health (points, maximum, percent), level and street cred with their experience, money (eddies), the wanted level (the police system's heat stage, the star state and whether the police chase V, beside the two quest facts for comparison), the vehicle V is in (mounted or not, which record, driver or passenger), an inventory summary (counts and quantities by item type, not a list; at most 1500 stacks are read, and total_stacks and truncated say when more were left; equipped counts the inventory's equipped items by type, which under an outfit are only the gear beneath it, so clothing lists per area what is equipped and what the area shows: the outfit, hidden, the equipped item or empty), and the scanner (whether V is in scanner mode, how far the scan is, and what the scanner is on). parts picks some of vitals, progress, money, heat, vehicle, inventory and scanner (default all). Read only; player_state has V's position and movement. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

## Behaviours

Routines that run inside the game at frame rate: a turntable, a smooth look, a glide along a walkable path, keeping a subject framed. Each streams its progress to the session's events and stops on `behave_stop`, the kill switch or loading a save.

### `behave_turntable`

**Turn showroom heads or rigs continuously.** A behaviour: the showroom's heads (or their light rigs, or both) turn continuously at deg_per_s, in the game at frame rate, until revolutions are done, max_s passes or behave_stop; then they turn back where they were unless return is false. Its progress and its end are in session_events.

- **Command:** `behave.turntable`, the bridge method `behave.turntable`
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop with its id (the heads turn back); the kill switch and loading a save stop it too.
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | `pieces`, `rigs`, `both` | pieces (default), rigs or both. |
| `pieces` | array of integer | at most 24 items; each 0 to 23 | Which heads by lineup index (default all). |
| `deg_per_s` | number | -360 to 360 | Degrees a second, -360 to 360 (positive turns them to their left). Default 30. |
| `revolutions` | number | 0.01 to 100 | Stop after this many turns, 0.01 to 100. |
| `return` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Turn them back where they were at the end (default true). |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_look`

**Turn V's view over time.** A behaviour: V's view turns towards a point (at) or to yaw and pitch (absolute degrees; turn for relative) over duration_s through the game's own look-at, watched each tick until it is within tolerance_deg (reached) or runs out (not_reached: the player's own mouse or stick breaks a look, as it breaks the game's). Normal play only.

- **Command:** `behave.look`, the bridge method `behave.look`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** behave_stop ends it; player_look back to the earlier angles (in player_state) turns the view back.
- **Refusals:** [`behaviour_limit`](#refusal-behaviour-limit), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`player_busy`](#refusal-player-busy), [`user_took_over`](#refusal-user-took-over)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point to look at [x, y, z]. |
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | The view's yaw, degrees (0 along the world's +Y, counter-clockwise). |
| `pitch` | number | -85 to 85 | The view's pitch, degrees (up positive), -85 to 85. |
| `turn` | object | the fields below | A relative turn instead of absolute angles. |
| `turn.yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Turn by this yaw, degrees. |
| `turn.pitch` | number | -170 to 170 | Tilt by this pitch, degrees. |
| `duration_s` | number | 0.05 to 5 | How long the turn takes, 0.05 to 5 s. Default 1. |
| `tolerance_deg` | number | 0.2 to 10 | Close enough, 0.2 to 10 degrees. Default 2. |
| `max_s` | number | 0.1 to 600 | Stop after this many seconds, 0.1 to 600. Default 60 (a look: its duration plus 5 s; a glide: at most 30). |
| `every_ticks` | integer | 1 to 60 | Act every this many game ticks, 1 to 60 (default 2 for a turntable, 3 for keep_framed, else 1). |

### `behave_glide_path`

**Glide V along a walkable path.** Glides V along a human-navmesh path with a per-tick teleport and a movement hold, released on stop, failure, timeout or human takeover. Traffic risk is unknown while lane containment is uncommissioned: the answer and catch-up carry a warning; inspect the path for traffic. Navmesh is not road-safety proof.

### `behave_keep_framed`

**Keep a subject framed as the camera moves.** A behaviour: keeps a subject at a frame position (at, window heights from the centre; default the centre) while the camera moves. subject piece: a showroom head is moved onto the camera's view ray at distance_m (default its distance at the start), facing the camera, exactly from the camera's pose (needs the showroom permission too). subject v: in photo mode, V's placement (left/right, up/down) is steered from a measured response, as photo_frame measures it, refined after each step. Stops at max_s or on behave_stop; its stop event carries the undo.

| `at.y` | number | -0.5 to 0.5 | Down, window heights from the centre. |
| `distance_m` | number | 0.3 to 20 | A head's eyes this far from the camera, 0.3 to 20 m (default: as at the start). |

### `behave_stop`

**Stop behaviours.** Stops one behaviour (id) or all of them. Each stops on the next game tick and gives back what it held (a turntable turns its heads back, a glide gives V her movement back); session_events says how each ended.

**List running behaviours.** The behaviours running in the game now: id, kind, target, state, how long they have run and a summary (how far a head has turned, a glide travelled, a look's remaining angle).

## Live direction

The DM toolkit: bring props, vehicles and lights in, change doors and vehicles, play sounds and a radio, send a message toast or a real incoming call, put an XF quest in the HUD's tracker, show the game's own banners and quest toasts, and arm watchers that fire micro-actions inside the game without the agent. All of it is in the `dm` class, never saved, and given back by each answer's undo, the kill switch, the pause, a handover or loading a save.

### `world_spawn`

**Bring in a prop or a vehicle.** Brings a prop or a vehicle into the world near V: a prop from an entity template (the depot path of a .ent file) or a record, a vehicle from its record (such as Vehicle.v_standard2_archer_hella_player), placed offset metres from V along her facing (default two metres ahead) or at a world point within 60 m, snapped to the ground below unless ground is false, facing yaw, or V with face_v. It is never saved: world_despawn, the kill switch, a pause, a handover or loading a save removes it, and game_save refuses while one exists. At most 24 spawned things (props, vehicles and lights together). Answers its handle (use spawn:&lt;n> as a target in other commands) and its entity id at once; the thing appears a moment later. Unknown traffic classification proceeds with traffic_risk unknown and a warning; nearest pavement is unavailable and this is not safe placement proof. Needs Codeware and the -writes package's toolkit scripts. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `world.spawn`, the bridge method `world.spawn`
- **Permission:** Direct the scene (`write-dm`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo is world_despawn of its handle; the kill switch, a pause, a handover and loading a save remove everything the bridge spawned.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), `limit`, [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), `record_missing`, `template_missing`, [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`script_layer_missing`](#refusal-script-layer-missing), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `prop`, `vehicle` | prop (the default) or vehicle. |
| `template` | string | at most 200 characters | A prop's entity template: its depot path ending in .ent. |
| `record` | string | at most 128 characters | A TweakDB record to spawn (a vehicle's, or a prop's), such as Vehicle.v_standard2_archer_hella_player. |
| `appearance` | string | at most 64 characters | An appearance by name (default: the template's or record's own). |
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point [x, y, z] (within 60 m of V) instead of offset. |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | A place relative to V: forward, right and up in metres from her feet (default two metres ahead). |
| `offset.forward` | number | -60 to 60 | Metres along V's facing (negative: behind her), -60 to 60. Default 2. |
| `offset.right` | number | -60 to 60 | Metres to V's right (negative: left), -60 to 60. Default 0. |
| `offset.up` | number | -20 to 20 | Metres up from her feet (negative: down), -20 to 20. Default 0. |
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Its facing in degrees (the game's yaw: 0 faces north, 90 faces west). |
| `face_v` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Face V. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 48 characters | A name for it in answers and events. |
| `ground` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Snap to the ground below the place (default true); false puts it exactly where asked. |
| `when` | object | the fields below | Conditions compared on each executing game frame |
| `when.phase` | string | `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `main_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `character_menu` | Required phase |
| `when.vehicle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be mounted/unmounted |
| `when.combat` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be in/out of combat |
| `when.photo_mode` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Photo mode must be active/inactive |
| `when.spawned` | array of integer | 1 to 16 items; each 1 to 2147483647 | Returned spawn handles that must still resolve |

### `world_despawn`

**Remove spawned props and vehicles.** Removes a prop or vehicle the bridge brought in (its handle, from world_spawn), or every one with all (lights are removed with light_remove). The answer's undo (or undo_all, one per thing) spawns each again where it stood, under a new handle.

- **Permission:** Direct the scene (`write-dm`)

- **Undo:** The result's undo spawns it again where it stood (a new handle); undo_all does so for each when several were removed.

**What the bridge brought in.** The props, vehicles and lights the bridge has brought in this session: each one's handle, entity id, kind, label and where it stands now, and the sounds it tracks. Changes nothing.

**Open, close, lock or seal a door.** Opens, closes, locks, unlocks, seals or unseals the door V is looking at (target look_at), a door by its entity id, or one the bridge spawned: open true unlocks and unseals it first (as the game's own quest actions do), and an open door can't be locked or sealed in the same call. The first state each door had is remembered: the kill switch, a pause and a handover put every door back, and game_save refuses while one is changed. ### `phone_call`

**Ring V with a call.** Rings V's phone with a real incoming call from a contact the player has (ids from phone_state {contacts: true}; the game's own ring, name and picture). When the player answers it (or at once, with auto_answer: the bridge answers a call it placed as the phone's own answer key does, so no key press is needed), the bridge starts the call and shows the lines one after another as subtitles in the call's style, then ends the call; a rejected call, a missed one and a hang-up are events (dm.phone). mode audio (the default) shows the contact's picture; video asks for the holocall frame, which the game fills only with a camera feed it stages for its own calls. A caller the journal doesn't hold is refused: the phone's code would run on a missing contact. Refused while the phone is blocked (combat, a story scene). One call at a time. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `phone.call`, the bridge method `phone.call`
- **Permission:** Direct the scene (`write-dm`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo is phone_end, which ends the ring or the call; an unanswered call ends by itself.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`busy`](#refusal-busy), `contact_unknown`, `phone_blocked`, [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| `lines[].text` (required) | string | 1 to 300 characters | The words, up to 300 characters. |

### `light_spawn`

**Bring in a light.** Brings in a light: an entity whose template holds a light component, set to the colour, intensity (in the component's own units), radius and, for a spot, the cone (inner and outer, full angles in degrees), placed like a prop. With no template it uses the XF light carrier, which is not built yet (carrier_missing); name a template that holds a light component (for example a lamp's), or bring a lamp in with world_spawn and steer it with light_set. pattern sets the engine's flicker or one the tick drives (pulse, strobe, broken, candle; at most 4 at once). Never saved; counts among the 24 spawned things, at most 8 lights. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `light.spawn`, the bridge method `light.spawn`
- **Permission:** Direct the scene (`write-dm`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo is light_remove of its handle; the kill switch, a pause, a handover and loading a save remove every light.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), `limit`, [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `carrier_missing`, `template_missing`, [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | at most 200 characters | An entity template with a light component: its depot path ending in .ent. |
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point [x, y, z] (within 60 m of V) instead of offset. |
| `offset` | object | the fields below | A place relative to V: forward, right and up in metres from her feet (default two metres ahead). |
| `offset.forward` | number | -60 to 60 | Metres along V's facing (negative: behind her), -60 to 60. Default 2. |
| `offset.right` | number | -60 to 60 | Metres to V's right (negative: left), -60 to 60. Default 0. |
| `offset.up` | number | -20 to 20 | Metres up from her feet (negative: down), -20 to 20. Default 0. |
| `yaw` | number | -360 to 360 | Its facing in degrees (the game's yaw: 0 faces north, 90 faces west). |
| `face_v` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Face V. |
| `colour` | string or array of integer | matches `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$`; or exactly 3 items; each 0 to 255 | A colour: #rrggbb or [red, green, blue] (0 to 255). |
| `intensity` | number | 0 to 100000 | The component's intensity, 0 to 100000. Default 100. |
| `radius` | number | 0.1 to 50 | The reach in metres, 0.1 to 50. Default 8. |
| `inner` | number | 1 to 179 | A spot's inner cone angle, 1 to 179. |
| `outer` | number | 1 to 179 | A spot's outer cone angle, 1 to 179 (at least inner). |
| `pattern` | string or object | `steady`, `flicker`, `pulse`, `strobe`, `broken`, `candle`; or the fields below | How the light behaves over time: a name, or {kind, period, low, strength, seed}. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 48 characters | A name for it in answers and events. |
| `when` | object | the fields below | Conditions compared on each executing game frame |
| `when.phase` | string | `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `main_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `character_menu` | Required phase |
| `when.vehicle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be mounted/unmounted |
| `when.combat` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be in/out of combat |
| `when.photo_mode` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Photo mode must be active/inactive |
| `when.spawned` | array of integer | 1 to 16 items; each 1 to 2147483647 | Returned spawn handles that must still resolve |
