### `watch_arm`

**Arm an in-game watcher.** Arms a watcher that runs inside the game and, when its condition holds, logs an event (dm.watch) and runs up to 8 micro-actions (bridge commands, each with its own delay_s) without the agent: enter or leave (V inside or outside radius_m of a point or an entity), gaze (V looks at an entity for seconds, by a cone or by the game's look-at), weapon, combat or vehicle (the edge on or off), interact (V uses something; caption part, target), choice (V picks a dialogue choice; caption part, index), timer (seconds after arming) or clock (the game's time of day passes a mark). repeat keeps it armed with a cooldown; it ends at expires_s (default 600, at most 3600), when it fires (unless repeat), by watch_disarm, the kill switch, a pause, a handover and a load. At most 16 at once. A micro-action goes through the bridge's own gates like any request; saving, loading, the kill switch, handing over and the creator's buttons are never allowed, and a watcher armed by an action carries no actions of its own. The pick of a dialogue choice is inferred from the game's choice list going away [unverified]. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `watch.arm`, the bridge method `watch.arm`
- **Permission:** Direct the scene (`write-dm`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo is watch_disarm; a watcher also ends when it fires (unless repeat), expires, by the kill switch and when a save loads.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), `too_many`, [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,48}$` | A short id (default w1, w2, ...); an armed id is replaced. |
| `kind` (required) | string | `enter`, `leave`, `gaze`, `weapon`, `combat`, `vehicle`, `interact`, `choice`, `timer`, `clock` | What it watches. |
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point (enter, leave). |
| `target` | string | at most 40 characters; matches `^(any\|(?:dynamic\|static): '[0-9]{1,20}'\|EntityID\([0-9]{1,20}\)\|[0-9]{1,20}\|spawn:[1-9][0-9]{0,5})$` | An entity (spawn:&lt;n> or an entity id) for enter, leave, gaze and interact; any for interact. |
| `radius_m` | number | 0.5 to 500 | Enter and leave: the radius, 0.5 to 500. Default 5. |
| `seconds` | number | 0 to 3600 | Gaze: the dwell; timer: the delay (0.1 to 3600). |
| `cone_deg` | number | 1 to 60 | Gaze: the half-angle of the cone, 1 to 60. Default 12. |
| `max_m` | number | 1 to 300 | Gaze: the farthest distance, 1 to 300. Default 30. |
| `look_at` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Gaze: use the game's look-at instead of the cone. |
| `edge` | string | `on`, `off` | Weapon, combat, vehicle: on (the default) or off. |
| `now` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Fire at once when it already holds on the first sample (default true except for leave). |
| `caption` | string | at most 64 characters | Interact and choice: part of the caption (case does not matter). |
| `index` | integer | 0 to 9 | Choice: the index of the choice, 0 to 9. |
| `clock` | string | matches `^[0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]$` | Clock: the time of day as HH:MM. |
| `expires_s` | number | 1 to 3600 | Seconds until it ends, 1 to 3600. Default 600. |
| `repeat` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Keep it armed after it fires. |
| `cooldown_s` | number | 0 to 600 | The least seconds between two firings, 0 to 600. Default 2. |
| `hz` | number | 1 to 30 | How often it is sampled, 1 to 30 a second. |
| `actions` | array of object | at most 8 items | Up to 8 micro-actions, run in order when it fires. |
| `actions[].method` (required) | string | at most 64 characters; matches `^[a-z]+(\.[a-z]+)+$` | A bridge method such as notify.show or audio.play. |
| `actions[].params` | any | any | Its parameters, an object (under 4 KiB). |
| `actions[].delay_s` | number | 0 to 30 | Wait this long first, 0 to 30. |
| `when` | object | the fields below | Conditions compared on each executing game frame |
| `when.phase` | string | `gameplay`, `photo_mode`, `main_menu`, `menu`, `paused`, `character_menu` | Required phase |
| `when.vehicle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be mounted/unmounted |
| `when.combat` | boolean | `true`, `false` | V must be in/out of combat |
| `when.photo_mode` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Photo mode must be active/inactive |
| `when.spawned` | array of integer | 1 to 16 items; each 1 to 2147483647 | Returned spawn handles that must still resolve |

## World

Read the world's state, probe the ground and streaming around V, and set the clock, the weather, a freeze or XF map pins.

### `world_time_set`

**Set the time of day.** Sets the in-game clock (hours, minutes, seconds) while V is in the world or the appearance screen is open (to compare the screen's light at different times of day without leaving it), or restores an exact earlier time with total_seconds. In photo mode it sets photo mode's own time of day instead (the Environment tab's slider, hours and minutes only; a photo-mode setting, so the photo write class must be allowed too). Whether the world's clock is as before once photo mode closes is not established yet (game_status's world_time_seconds shows it). target photo or world names the clock: a photo-mode undo carries target photo, so replayed after photo mode closes it changes nothing rather than the world's clock. Changing the world clock can trigger timed events in quests, so use a disposable save.

- **Command:** `world.time.set`, the bridge method `world.time.set`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo: the world's clock with total_seconds (target world), or photo mode's time of day in hours and minutes (target photo), which changes nothing once photo mode has closed.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_in_photo_mode`](#refusal-not-in-photo-mode), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hours` | integer | 0 to 23 | Hour, 0 to 23. |
| `minutes` | integer | 0 to 59 | Minute, 0 to 59. |
| `seconds` | integer | 0 to 59 | Second, 0 to 59. |
| `total_seconds` | integer | 0 to 2147483647 | An exact earlier time from a previous result's undo (the world's clock only). |
| `target` | string | `world`, `photo` | Which clock: world (refused in photo mode) or photo (photo mode's own time of day; outside photo mode nothing changes). Default: photo in photo mode, else world. |

### `world_pause`

**Freeze the world.** Freezes everything around V (paused: true), the way the appearance screen does, or unfreezes it (paused: false). Only in normal play: photo mode and the appearance screen already freeze the world.

- **Command:** `world.pause`, the bridge method `world.pause`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** world.pause with paused: false; the kill switch also unfreezes.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paused` (required) | boolean | `true`, `false` | true freezes, false unfreezes. |

### `world_pin`

**Place an XF map pin.** Temporary test feature (bridge 0.5.3). Places a map pin with an XF badge and a label, shown on the world map (with the label in its tooltip), on the minimap and in the world through walls, the way the game shows its own markers: the game's own pin icon, with the XF badge above it and the label on the pin's name line. Give exactly one of position [x, y, z] (a world point in metres, as game_status and showroom_state report them), piece (a showroom head's index: the pin's point is at its crown, 0.12 m above its eyes by default, and the game draws its marker just above that point; placed there, so turning the head leaves it and clearing the heads removes it) or at: "v" (above where V stands now). label names it (1-48 characters). variant picks the game's pin type whose map filter and icon it uses: custom (default; the one the minimap draws for any placed pin), interaction (in the world only), apartment, clothes or default. lift_m raises it (metres; default 0 at a position, 0.12 above a head's eyes, 0.45 above V). ui_state's pins[].xf_mark gives where the XF mark is (px, its top-left corner in window pixels) and where the pin's own point is (point_px). The answer's pins list which views have drawn each pin so far (drawn_by: world, minimap, world_map), and the plugin log names each one the first time. At most 8 pins. world.pin.clear, the kill switch and loading a save remove them.

- **Command:** `world.pin`, the bridge method `world.pin`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** world.pin.clear with the result's id; the kill switch and loading a save also remove every XF pin.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), `too_many_pins`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`not_spawned_yet`](#refusal-not-spawned-yet), `pin_refused`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point [x, y, z] in metres. |
| `piece` | integer | 0 to 23 | A showroom head's index (0 to 23), from showroom_state. |
| `at` | string | `v` | v: above where V stands now. |
| `label` (required) | string | 1 to 400 characters | The pin's name, 1 to 48 characters (longer is cut). |
| `variant` | string | `custom`, `interaction`, `apartment`, `clothes`, `default` | The game's pin type it borrows its map filter and icon from. Default custom. |
| `lift_m` | number | -5 to 5 | Metres above the point (-5 to 5). |

### `world_state`

**Read the world's state.** The world as it is now: the clock (day, time, paused, time dilation, the bridge's freeze), the rain (type, intensity, puddles, moisture), the weather state's name and this world's weather states (with Codeware; without it only the rain is readable), named quest facts (facts: their values, read only), and in photo mode its own time, weather, NPC and game-speed rows with their options. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `world.state`, the bridge method `world.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)

### `world_probe`

**Probe the world at points.** Observe only: at each point (points, up to 16, or a ring around V with around_v), whether the walkable ground around it is loaded (streamed), the nearest walkable point within radius_m, the ground below (a static-geometry ray down_m down) and the ceiling above, and the distance from V. Also returns traffic_check (lane classification and nearest pavement currently INCONCLUSIVE, radius_m is the requested search radius) and the real V-to-point road_boundary_intersection query. Boundary false cannot prove off-road; it excludes disabled/GPS-only lanes and is not lane containment. For choosing a place before placement; nothing is moved or loaded.

- **Command:** `world.probe`, the bridge method `world.probe`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | array of array of number | 1 to 16 items; each exactly 3 items | World points to probe. |
| `around_v` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Probe V's place and a ring around her instead of points. |
| `ring_m` | number | 0.5 to 50 | The ring's radius, 0.5 to 50 m. Default 3. |
| `count` | integer | 1 to 15 | Points on the ring, 1 to 15. Default 8. |
| `radius_m` | number | 0.2 to 10 | How far to look for walkable ground from each point, 0.2 to 10 m. Default 2. |
| `down_m` | number | 0.5 to 100 | How far below each point the ground ray looks, 0.5 to 100 m. Default 10. |
| `clearance_m` | number | 0.05 to 3 | Also cast eight level rays this long from each point and report which are blocked (free space), 0.05 to 3 m. |
| `sight_from` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Also check the sight line from this world point to each point (static geometry between). |

### `world_weather_set`

**Set the weather.** Holds one of this world's weather states (name, as world_state lists them, blending over blend_s seconds), which stops the game's own weather cycle, or gives the weather back to the cycle (cycle: true, with or without a name). Needs Codeware (detected, never installed). Refused in a story scene (quest_scene), where the story may hold the weather; elsewhere a quest's own weather hold can still win, and giving the weather back to the cycle ends such a hold too (the answer's note says so). The answer carries the undo (the earlier state and the cycle back on); the kill switch does the same. A save made meanwhile would keep the weather, so the save lock stays on and game_save refuses until it is undone.

- **Command:** `world.weather.set`, the bridge method `world.weather.set`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo sets the earlier weather and turns the game's cycle back on; the kill switch does the same.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`quest_scene`](#refusal-quest-scene), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` | The weather state, such as 24h_weather_rain. |
| `blend_s` | number | 0 to 60 | Blend time, 0 to 60 seconds. Default 2. |
| `cycle` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Give the weather back to the game's own cycle (after setting name, if given). |

### `world_events`

**Read the passive world event feed.** Bounded read-only feed in every build, also during loads. since is an inclusive sequence cursor; resume at next, including across filtered rows. Kinds: session, death (including defeated and knockdown), combat, heat, dialogue, journal, fact, call. Each carries QPC s, nullable game_time_s, world_generation, session_counter and dropped since its kind's last kept event. 2048 entries, 20 admissions per kind per QPC second; 100 records and 48 KiB per page. missed and evicted expose retention loss; dropped counts rate and contention loss. Codeware supplies early session/load/save callbacks. Without it coverage.session_callbacks is script_layer_only, with no early load/start or save notifications. Dialogue copies at most two hubs/four choices/48 characters and marks truncation; partner is unavailable because the checked hub schema provides no entity. Journal paths cap at 16 segments and mark path_complete. Source/offline until commissioned. Optional recorder events channel carries these same envelopes; game.catchup includes them in channels.events. Cursors restart with the bridge process/session.

- **Command:** `world.events`, the bridge method `world.events`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`bad_params`](#refusal-bad-params)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | integer | 0 to 1000000000000 | Inclusive cursor returned as next |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 100 | Page size, also bounded to 48 KiB |
| `kinds` | array of string | at most 8 items; each `session`, `death`, `combat`, `heat`, `dialogue`, `journal`, `fact`, `call` | Filter to these event families |

### `world_facts`

**Read quest facts in a batch.** Reads many named quest facts in one call: facts (a list of at most 128 names) and/or preset. The preset main_story is the 93 main-story facts of the 2.31 quest data (research/story-engine/main-story-facts.json; the answer also groups them by category), final_boards the 29 the game's final boards read. Names are letters, digits, _ and . only. A fact the game never set reads 0, the same as one set to 0. Read only; world_state reads up to 16 facts beside the clock and weather. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

- **Command:** `world.facts`, the bridge method `world.facts`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facts` | array of string | at most 128 items; each at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | Quest fact names to read (at most 128). |
| `preset` | string | `main_story`, `final_boards` | A named list of facts, read with any extra facts: main_story (The main-story facts of the 2.31 quest data (93), grouped in the answer by category.) final_boards (The facts the game's own final boards read (29): whose fate matters for the ending.) |

### `world_district`

**Read V's district.** Where V is in Night City's own terms, from the game's district system (the one the minimap and the police use): the innermost area, and above it the subdistrict and district (a place such as Kabuki_NoTellMotel inside Kabuki inside Watson), each with its name, type, crime multiplier and gangs, the police preset in force, Dogtown and Badlands flags, and the map's own location text as a cross-check. District is not position: player_state has the coordinates. Refused with no_district for a moment after a load, until the game has told its district system where V is. Read only. With no world to read it is refused game_loading (the bridge's gate, on the main menu, between sessions and during a load) or, if the gate is open but the game has no world yet, game_not_ready.

- **Command:** `world.district`, the bridge method `world.district`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`no_district`](#refusal-no-district), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_loading`](#refusal-game-loading)

No parameters.

## Wardrobe, clothing and cyberware

Read and change what V wears and her cyberware, through the game's own equipment requests. Off in every build until writes to V's inventory are approved.

### `inventory_equip`

**Equip a clothing item on V.** Equips a clothing item on V by its item record (for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01), as the inventory screen does, and waits until the slot shows it. With add_if_missing, an item V doesn't have is added to V's inventory first (and remembered, so inventory_unequip can remove it again). Clothing slots only (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit); only in normal play, not in combat or a scene. When an active wardrobe outfit (or a hidden area) decides what the slot shows, the item is equipped but doesn't draw: the answer says so (hidden_by_outfit, outfit) and wardrobe_equip is the next step. Needs the inventory permission, which the bridge's settings keep off until the maintainer allows it.

- **Command:** `inventory.equip`, the bridge method `inventory.equip`
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo equips the earlier item's exact copy again (its id), or empties the slot (removing an item the bridge added); loading a save also undoes it.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | The item record, for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01. |
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | The clothing slot, checked against the item's own (optional). |
| `add_if_missing` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Add the item to V's inventory if V doesn't have it. Default false. |
| `id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The exact copy to equip, as an undo names it (the decimal identity the game gave); without it, any copy of the record. When V no longer has that copy, another copy is equipped and the answer says exact: false. |

### `inventory_list`

**List the clothing V owns.** Observe only: the clothing items in V's own inventory, one entry per copy: its item record (inventory_equip's item), clothing slot (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit), id (that exact copy's identity, inventory_equip's id), its name in the game's language and whether V wears it now; count says how many there are in all, listed how many the answer carries. slot lists one slot only. Nothing is changed, and the inventory permission isn't needed. Items stored only in the wardrobe aren't listed (wardrobe_state shows those).

- **Command:** `inventory.list`, the bridge method `inventory.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | Only this clothing slot. |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 200 | At most this many entries, 1 to 200. Default 100. |

### `wardrobe_state`

**Read V's wardrobe outfit.** The wardrobe outfit V wears (set 1-7, or 0 for none) and, for each clothing area (Head, Face, OuterChest, InnerChest, Legs, Feet), what it shows: outfit (the outfit's item), hidden (nothing: the outfit leaves the area empty, or headgear is hidden), equipped or empty; plus what is equipped there and the wardrobe's stored outfits. An active outfit overrides what the equipment slots show, which is why an equipped helmet can stay invisible. manager says who decides: wardrobe (a wardrobe outfit, set 1-7), script (a script mod's outfit system, named in managed_by when known, such as EquipmentEx: active is true while set is 0, and the wardrobe's own requests don't reach it) or none (what is equipped shows); suspended_by_bridge says the bridge took an outfit off (wardrobe_equip resume puts it back); script_outfit is Equipment-EX's outfit when it is installed (its version, active and its parts: outfit slot, item and the item's exact identity; available false with why when the installed Equipment-EX lacks a function the bridge calls, and then only suspend and resume drive it).

- **Command:** `wardrobe.state`, the bridge method `wardrobe.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

No parameters.

### `wardrobe_equip`

**Change V's wardrobe outfit.** Changes what V's clothing shows through the wardrobe, as the wardrobe screen does (the equipment system's own requests; stored outfits are never edited or saved): set applies outfit 1-7; clear takes the outfit off, so V shows what is equipped; item shows that clothing item in its area of the active outfit (the item must be in V's inventory or the wardrobe); area with show equipped makes that area show what is equipped there, and show hidden hides it; restore (the undo) puts back exactly the outfit and each area a snapshot recorded (with no outfit too: each area's hidden state; the same copy of each item when V still has it, and everything it still can, naming what neither the wardrobe nor V's inventory has any more in not_restored); suspend takes the outfit off with the story's own request, whoever manages it (the wardrobe or a script mod's outfit system such as EquipmentEx), so equipped clothing draws, and resume puts that outfit back. Under a script mod's outfit system, item puts the item into that outfit where the bridge can drive it (Equipment-EX: its own outfit system, as its screen does; the undo restores its parts exactly), and suspend and resume work for any; the rest is refused (outfit_managed_elsewhere). Waits until the wardrobe shows the change. Only in normal play, not in combat or a scene. Needs the inventory permission; the kill switch puts back the wardrobe as it was before the bridge's first change.

- **Command:** `wardrobe.equip`, the bridge method `wardrobe.equip`
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo (wardrobe_equip with restore, or resume after suspend) puts the outfit and every area back exactly; the kill switch resumes a suspended outfit and restores the wardrobe as it was before the bridge's first change.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`no_active_outfit`](#refusal-no-active-outfit), [`outfit_managed_elsewhere`](#refusal-outfit-managed-elsewhere), [`script_outfit_api_changed`](#refusal-script-outfit-api-changed), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | integer | 1 to 7 | Apply this wardrobe outfit (1-7; wardrobe_state lists the stored ones). |
| `clear` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: take the active outfit off. |
| `item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | Show this clothing item record in its area of the active outfit, for example Items.Helmet_01_basic_01. |
| `area` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet` | The clothing area for show. |
| `show` | string | `equipped`, `hidden` | With area: equipped (the area shows what is equipped there) or hidden (nothing). |
| `suspend` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: take the outfit off for now with the story's own request (works under the wardrobe and script outfit systems alike), so equipped clothing draws; the undo is resume. |
| `resume` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: put back the outfit the bridge took off with suspend. |
| `restore` | object | the fields below | A wardrobe_equip answer's undo: the outfit (0 none) and what each area showed. |
| `restore.set` (required) | integer | 0 to 7 | The outfit that was active, 0 for none. |
| `restore.slots` | array of object | at most 6 items | What each area showed. |
| `restore.slots[].area` (required) | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet` | The clothing area. |
| `restore.slots[].item` | string | at most 128 characters | The outfit's item in the area (empty: none). |
| `restore.slots[].id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The item's exact identity as the snapshot reported it (0.6.1: the same copy is put back when V still has it). |
| `restore.slots[].hidden` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether the area was hidden. |
| `restore.script_outfit` | object | the fields below | A script outfit system's outfit when the snapshot was taken (Equipment-EX): on or off, and its parts. |
| `restore.script_outfit.active` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether that outfit was on. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts` | array of object | at most 64 items | Each outfit slot in use and its item. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].slot` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The outfit slot record, e.g. OutfitSlots.Head. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters | The item record. |
| `restore.script_outfit.parts[].id` | string | at most 20 characters; matches `^[0-9]{1,20}$` | The item's exact identity as the snapshot reported it (0.6.1). |

### `inventory_unequip`

**Take off a clothing item.** Takes off what V wears in one clothing slot (slot), or the given item (item), and waits until the slot is empty. remove_added also takes the item out of V's inventory, but only an item the bridge itself added this session. Needs the inventory permission.

- **Command:** `inventory.unequip`, the bridge method `inventory.unequip`
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** the result's undo equips the earlier item again.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`not_added_by_bridge`](#refusal-not-added-by-bridge), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | string | `Head`, `Face`, `OuterChest`, `InnerChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit` | The clothing slot to empty. |
| `item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$` | The item record to take off (instead of slot). |
| `remove_added` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Also remove the item from V's inventory if the bridge added it (with item). Default false. |

### `cyberware_state`

**Read V's cyberware.** What each of V's cyberware areas holds (ArmsCW, HandsCW, EyesCW, FaceCW, FrontalCortexCW, SystemReplacementCW, NervousSystemCW, CardiovascularSystemCW, ImmuneSystemCW, IntegumentarySystemCW, MusculoskeletalSystemCW, LegsCW), slot by slot with each item's record and name; for the arms, the chain the character creator's holster state follows (the ArmsCW item's holstered item and its appearance, such as holstered_mantis, and the creator group that draws it), what the right-arm and weapon slots hold now, drawn (the arm cyberware is out, by the rule cyberware changes are refused by), and whether a no-arm-cyberware effect is on; V's humanity. areas limits the list.

- **Command:** `cyberware.state`, the bridge method `cyberware.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `areas` | array of string | 1 to 12 items; each `ArmsCW`, `HandsCW`, `EyesCW`, `FaceCW`, `FrontalCortexCW`, `SystemReplacementCW`, `NervousSystemCW`, `CardiovascularSystemCW`, `ImmuneSystemCW`, `IntegumentarySystemCW`, `MusculoskeletalSystemCW`, `LegsCW` | Only these areas (default all). |

### `cyberware_equip`

**Equip a cyberware item.** Puts a cyberware item into its area's slot through the game's own equipment request, as a ripperdoc's screen does (the earlier item in that slot comes out first): item is its record (Items.StrongArms, Items.MantisBlades, Items.NanoWires, Items.ProjectileLauncher, ...), slot the slot (default the first empty one), add_if_missing adds it to V's inventory first and remembers it. Only in normal play, outside combat and scenes; while the arm cyberware is drawn (after photo mode it stays drawn) the tools holster it first with the game's own request (holster_first: false refuses arms_drawn instead); the game's own equip requirements are checked before anything changes (not_equippable leaves nothing added). The answer reads the slot back and carries the undo (the exact earlier copy back, with a copy the bridge added removed, or the slot emptied and an added item removed); if the slot can't be read back, equipped is unknown and the undo is still given. V's look and stats change until the undo, the kill switch or a load; the save lock is held meanwhile and game_save refuses until it is undone. In the inventory class, off unless allowed.

- **Command:** `cyberware.equip`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo puts the earlier item back, or empties the slot and removes an item the bridge added; loading the save undoes it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`arms_drawn`](#refusal-arms-drawn), [`not_equippable`](#refusal-not-equippable), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | The cyberware item's record, such as Items.MantisBlades. |
| `slot` | integer | 0 to 9 | The slot, 0 to 9 (default: the first empty one). |
| `add_if_missing` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Add the item to V's inventory first if V doesn't have it (removed again by the undo). |
| `id` | string | matches `^[0-9]{1,24}$` | The exact copy to equip, as an undo names it (digits). |
| `remove_added_item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | After the equip, remove the copy of this record the bridge added (a swap's undo gives it). |
| `holster_first` | boolean | `true`, `false` | When V has her arm cyberware out, holster it first with the game's own request and then make the change (default true); false refuses arms_drawn instead. |

### `cyberware_unequip`

**Empty a cyberware slot.** Takes a cyberware item out of its slot through the game's own unequip request: area (ArmsCW, ...) and slot (one of the area's unlocked slots), or item (its record; its own slot is found). remove_added also removes an item the bridge itself added this session. Normal play only; while the arm cyberware is drawn the tools holster it first (holster_first: false refuses arms_drawn instead). The answer reads the slot back and carries the undo (the item equipped again).

- **Command:** `cyberware.unequip`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Change V's clothing (`write-inventory`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo equips the item again; loading the save undoes it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`not_safe_now`](#refusal-not-safe-now), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`not_in_inventory`](#refusal-not-in-inventory), [`call_failed`](#refusal-call-failed), [`arms_drawn`](#refusal-arms-drawn), [`not_added_by_bridge`](#refusal-not-added-by-bridge)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `area` | string | `ArmsCW`, `HandsCW`, `EyesCW`, `FaceCW`, `FrontalCortexCW`, `SystemReplacementCW`, `NervousSystemCW`, `CardiovascularSystemCW`, `ImmuneSystemCW`, `IntegumentarySystemCW`, `MusculoskeletalSystemCW`, `LegsCW` | The cyberware area. |
| `item` | string | at most 128 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$` | The item's record (instead of area). |
| `slot` | integer | 0 to 9 | The slot, 0 to 9 (default 0, or the item's slot). |
| `remove_added` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Also remove the item from V's inventory when the bridge added it (with item). |

## XF Finish Showroom

Spawn, light, turn and clear the showroom's mannequin heads for close-up finish checks. Nothing is saved: clearing, the kill switch or loading a save removes them.

### `showroom_spawn`

**Set out the finish showroom.** Spawns XF Finish Showroom's mannequin heads, one per makeup preset of a showroom build (its folder or manifest.json from tools/build_showroom_package.ts), each on a black pedestal: in an arc about the camera (default; every head faces it) or a row across the view, spacing_m apart, each head's eyes distance_m from the camera (in photo mode) or V's eyes, as photo_frame's distance_m measures to V, and at height_m above V's ground (default: the camera's height with the camera as anchor, so the heads look straight into it; a head's natural height with V as anchor). Needs Codeware in the game and the showroom's archive staged. Nothing is saved: showroom.clear, the kill switch or loading a save removes them.

- **Command:** `showroom.spawn`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.clear with what: pieces (or all); loading a save also removes them.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`showroom_missing`](#refusal-showroom-missing), `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_manifest_bad`, `showroom_not_staged`, [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | The showroom build's folder, or its manifest.json. Default (0.8.3): the XF Finish Showroom builds the game itself has staged (its archive/pc/mod folder), each with the manifest it ships inside the mod or, for an older build, this machine's build with the same bytes; every one is used, so a preset is found in whichever holds it. The answer's showroom_found names them. |
| `manifests` | array of string | 1 to 4 items; each at most 1024 characters | Several showroom builds' folders or manifests, to set out their presets together. |
| `presets` | array of string | 1 to 24 items; each at most 120 characters | Which presets, by name, preset ID or appearance, in lineup order. Default: all of them (at most 24). |
| `layout` | string | `arc`, `row` | arc (default): on a circle about the camera or V, each head facing it. row: a straight line across the view, all facing back along it. |
| `spacing_m` | number | 0.3 to 5 | Distance between neighbouring heads, 0.3 to 5 m. Default 0.7. |
| `distance_m` | number | 0.8 to 10 | How far each head's eyes are from the camera (or V's eyes), 0.8 to 10 m, in 3D. Default 2.5. |
| `height_m` | number | 0.5 to 3.2 | The heads' eye height above V's ground, 0.5 to 3.2 m. Default: the camera's height (anchor camera), else a head's natural 1.69 m. The pedestals reach 1.5 m below a head's natural place, so a head raised more than that ends in the air. |
| `lateral_m` | number | -5 to 5 | Shift the whole lineup to the right as the camera or V sees it (negative: left), -5 to 5 m. With distance_m equal to photo_frame's distance_m (the camera to V's face), a head at lateral 0.6 stands beside her on the same arc and appears at her scale. Default 0. |
| `anchor` | string | `camera`, `v` | camera (default in photo mode) or v (default in normal play). |
| `replace` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Remove the heads set out earlier first (default true). |
| `avoid_walls` | boolean | `true`, `false` | 0.7: check each head's eyes for free space and a clear sight line (world_probe) and move a blocked head back or sideways, saying so in moved_for_space. Default true. |

### `showroom_light`

**Light the finish showroom.** Spawns a light rig built from the game's own character-creator rig (native lumens, falloff, cones and shadows): rig creator (all 15 lights), creator_face (the 13 that reach the head, no shadows) or key (the key light alone). target each (default) gives every head its own rig in its own frame, so each gets the same light; piece lights one head; v lights V the same way, for the fidelity check. Rigs of neighbouring heads also light each other: the answer estimates by how much and warns above 5 %. Rigs stay put when heads turn, so a turn sweeps the highlights.

- **Command:** `showroom.light`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.clear with what: lights.
- **Refusals:** [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), [`showroom_missing`](#refusal-showroom-missing), `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_manifest_bad`, `showroom_not_staged`, [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | The showroom build's folder, or its manifest.json (its rig entity is used). Default (0.8.3): the staged builds, found as showroom_spawn finds them (the first one's rig). |
| `rig` | string | `creator`, `creator_face`, `key`, `none` | creator (default), creator_face, key, or none (remove every rig and keep the heads, as showroom_clear with what: lights). |
| `target` | string | `each`, `piece`, `v` | each (default): a rig per head; piece: the head given by piece; v: V herself. |
| `piece` | integer | 0 to 23 | The head's index in the lineup (0 is the first), with target piece. |
| `replace` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Remove the rigs placed earlier first (default true). |

### `showroom_rotate`

**Turn the showroom heads.** Turns showroom heads on their pedestals: yaw_deg relative to how they were set out (0 faces the camera or V as at spawn, positive turns them to their left), delta_deg from where they are now, or a turntable sweep from from_deg to to_deg in steps (default -60 to 60 in 7 steps), waiting settle_ms at each and, with capture, taking a screenshot of region (default the whole window) at each step. Light rigs don't turn, so the highlights sweep across each face. After a sweep the heads go back where they were unless return is false.

- **Command:** `showroom.rotate`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Set up the finish showroom (`write-showroom`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** showroom.rotate with yaw_deg 0 faces them as set out; a result's undo turns them back exactly.
- **Refusals:** `no_showroom`, [`no_such_piece`](#refusal-no-such-piece), [`not_spawned_yet`](#refusal-not-spawned-yet), `capture_no_window`, `capture_minimized`, `capture_not_foreground`, `capture_blank`, `capture_failed`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pieces` | array of integer | 1 to 24 items; each 0 to 23 | Which heads by lineup index (default all). |
| `yaw_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Yaw relative to how the heads were set out, -180 to 180. |
| `delta_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Turn by this much from where they are now, -180 to 180. |
| `sweep` | object | the fields below | A turntable sweep instead of one turn. |
| `sweep.from_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | First angle, relative to how the heads were set out. Default -60. |
| `sweep.to_deg` | number | -180 to 180 | Last angle. Default 60. |
| `sweep.steps` | integer | 1 to 36 | How many angles, 1 to 36, evenly spaced. Default 7. |
| `sweep.settle_ms` | integer | 0 to 5000 | Wait at each angle before the screenshot, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 400. |
| `sweep.capture` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Take a screenshot at each angle (default false). |

## NPC direction

Spawn XF actors (never saved), pick NPCs near V, and direct them: walk, follow, turn, place, speak (voiced, text or a caller's subtitle), look, set a face, gesture, and offer V dialogue choices whose pick comes back as an event. Releasing, the kill switch, the pause, a handover or loading a save gives everything back.

### `npc_list`

**List the NPCs near V.** The NPCs within radius_m of V (default 15, at most 40): each one's id (for npc_pick), record, distance and place, whether it is part of the street crowd, the look that defines it (appearance, colour variant) and which way it faces (yaw), whether it is protected (a quest character, a companion, a vendor, police, a child, a boss, or in a story scene) with the reasons, whether it is busy (sitting or leaning somewhere, fighting, hostile to V), whether npc_pick would take it (pickable: a plain passer-by of the street crowd, not busy), and which are the session's own. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `npc.list`, the bridge method `npc.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius_m` | number | 1 to 40 | How far from V to look, 1 to 40 metres. Default 15. |
| `max` | integer | 1 to 40 | At most this many, 1 to 40. Default 20. |

### `npc_pick`

**Pick an NPC near V.** Adopts one plain passer-by of the street crowd within 30 m of V (its id from npc_list, pickable) so the bridge can make it look at someone, change its face and say a line; it is never moved, placed, turned, given a gesture or a stance, or removed, and it keeps walking its own way. Anyone else is refused: protected NPCs (story characters, companions, vendors, police, children, bosses, anyone in a scene) and every NPC outside the street crowd (a quest may use one without marking it), and busy ones (sitting or leaning somewhere, fighting, hostile to V). A pick that becomes busy or protected later is given back at once (npc.auto_released), and its gaze, face and lines are taken back on its release, the kill switch, the pause and a handover; a load takes the NPC itself away. Answers the NPC's handle (p1, p2, ...). Changes nothing by itself.

- **Command:** `npc.pick`, the bridge method `npc.pick`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `npc_protected`, `npc_busy`, [`npc_not_found`](#refusal-npc-not-found), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `limit`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string | 1 to 64 characters | The NPC's id from npc_list. |

### `npc_status`

**Read the NPCs the bridge directs.** The session's actors and picked NPCs: each one's handle, cast or record, whether it has appeared, where it is, what it is doing (walking, following, turning), its lines still showing, its gaze, face and gesture; the dialogue choices showing, if any; and the substitutions still waiting for their moment (swaps), and the limits (5 actors, 4 picks, 30 m). Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `npc.status`, the bridge method `npc.status`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `npc_spawn`

**Bring in an XF actor.** Brings an XF actor into the world near V: cast is one of XF's own passers-by (a copy of an ordinary base-game civilian, never a story character), placed ahead_m metres along V's facing and side_m to her right (or at a world point), on walkable ground within 30 m of V, facing V (or face another NPC or face_point). out_of_sight lets the bridge choose a walkable spot V can't see (outside her view or behind a wall, min_m to max_m from her, 12 to 25 by default), so the actor walks in from somewhere rather than appearing; out_of_view waits until the spot isn't on screen. The masked casts cover the mouth with a mask or respirator, so lines without lip movement read naturally. By default the actor is friendly to V, can't be killed and has calm reactions; attitude neutral or hostile, immortal false and reactions game make a stand-in that can be shot (when a fight begins the bridge stops directing it and its own AI takes over, npc.handed_back; if it dies its body stays until released). The combat casts fighter_melee (bare fists, the safest first fixture) and fighter_pistol (a handgun) are copies of the base game's street-gang grunts instead of civilians: with attitude hostile (and immortal false if V may kill it) one fights V with its own AI, which a civilian never does; they keep their gang's own reactions, and by default they can't be killed so a test can't end by accident. engage true (with attitude hostile) also puts V in its own threat list at its first moment, the game's own route, in case the attitude alone doesn't start the fight; it never touches V. It is never saved: npc_release, the kill switch or loading a save removes it, and game_save refuses while one is out. At most 5 at once. Answers its handle (a1, a2, a3, ...) at once; npc.spawned follows in the event stream when it appears. Returns traffic_check at the final snapped point: lane containment and nearest pavement are INCONCLUSIVE. Needs Codeware and the -writes package's actor records.

- **Command:** `npc.spawn`, the bridge method `npc.spawn`
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo releases the actor (npc_release with how despawn); the kill switch and loading a save remove it too.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), `cast_unknown`, [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `record_missing`, [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), `not_walkable`, [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `limit`, `no_hidden_spot`, [`incident_unknown`](#refusal-incident-unknown), [`incident_limit`](#refusal-incident-limit), [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cast` (required) | string | `woman_corpo`, `man_corpo`, `woman_nightlife`, `man_youngster`, `woman_lowlife`, `man_lowlife`, `woman_masked`, `man_masked`, `fighter_melee`, `fighter_pistol`, `research_crowd_record`, `research_npc_base` | Which actor: woman_corpo, man_corpo, woman_nightlife, man_youngster, woman_lowlife or man_lowlife; woman_masked or man_masked wear a mask or respirator over the mouth (for lines without lip movement); fighter_melee and fighter_pistol are combat stand-ins (street-gang grunts: fists, handgun) that fight V when hostile; research_crowd_record and research_npc_base are for the session-9 comparison only. |
| `ahead_m` | number | -30 to 30 | Metres along V's facing (negative: behind her), -30 to 30. |
| `side_m` | number | -30 to 30 | Metres to V's right (negative: left), -30 to 30. Default 0. |
| `at_point` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point instead of ahead_m and side_m. |
| `face` | string | matches `^(v\|[ap][0-9]{1,5})$` | Face V ("v", the default) or another NPC (its handle). |
| `face_point` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Face this world point instead. |
| `appearance` | string | at most 96 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | One of the actor's appearances by name (default: the cast's own look, or random). |
| `variant` | integer | 0 to 31 | Which of the cast's own looks (npc_status lists them per cast), from 0. Default 0. |
| `out_of_view` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Appear only when the spot isn't on screen. |
| `out_of_sight` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Let the bridge pick a walkable spot V can't see (outside her view, or behind static geometry), instead of ahead_m or at_point. |
| `min_m` | number | 3 to 30 | With out_of_sight: at least this far from V, 3 to 30 m. Default 12. |
| `max_m` | number | 3 to 30 | With out_of_sight: at most this far from V, 3 to 30 m. Default 25. |
| `attitude` | string | `friendly`, `neutral`, `hostile` | How it stands towards V: friendly (the default), neutral or hostile. |
| `immortal` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether it can't be hurt or killed (default true); false makes a mortal stand-in. |
| `reactions` | string | `quiet`, `game` | quiet (the default: no crime or panic reactions) or game (an ordinary passer-by's own reactions). The combat casts always have their gang's own reactions (game); quiet is refused for them. |
| `engage` | boolean | `true`, `false` | With attitude hostile: also put V in the actor's own threat list at its first moment (the game's own route), in case the attitude alone doesn't start the fight. Default false. Never touches V. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 40 characters | The name its lines and dialogue choices show (default Stranger). |
| `incident` | string | 1 to 64 characters | Test build only: the id of a declared incident (incidents_declare) the new actor joins, so what it does counts in that incident and V's report carries it. Refused before anything is spawned when no such incident is open or it already holds five actors. |
| `incident_role` | string | 1 to 32 characters | With incident: the engine's own role name for the actor (default participant). |

### `npc_move`

**Walk an actor somewhere.** Sends one of the bridge's actors walking (or running) to V ("v"), to another NPC (its handle) or to a world point (to_point), stopping stop_m metres short (default 1.6); face_v sends V as the walk's facing target, off by default because the game keeps a facing target after the walk and a later walk then faces V (npc_turn after arriving faces her to V). It uses the game's own walking along walkable ground. npc.arrived follows when it gets there; npc.blocked when it makes no headway for 4 seconds (it keeps trying) or can't go on; npc.move_failed with the reason (no path, interrupted, or max_s passed, default 60). A new move replaces the last one. Picked NPCs aren't moved.

- **Command:** `npc.move`, the bridge method `npc.move`
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** npc_stop halts the actor where it is; it doesn't walk back.

|---|---|---|---|

| `to` | string | matches `^(v\|[ap][0-9]{1,5})$` | Where to: "v" or another NPC's handle. |
| `to_point` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A world point instead. |
| `gait` | string | `walk`, `run`, `sprint` | How it moves: walk (default), run or sprint. |

### `npc_say`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | string | matches `^[ap][0-9]{1,5}$` | The NPC V is talking to. |
| `title` | string | 1 to 40 characters | The widget's title (default the NPC's name). |
| `choices` | array of string | 2 to 4 items; each 1 to 90 characters | What V can say: 2 to 4 short lines. |
| `max_s` | number | 5 to 120 | Take the choices down after this many seconds, 5 to 120. Default 120. |
| `withdraw` | integer | 1 to 2147483647 | Take down the choices with this hub number (an earlier answer's hub) instead. |

### `npc_release`

**Release an NPC.** Ends what the bridge does with an NPC: its lines, gaze, face, gesture, walk and dialogue choices are taken back, then an actor is removed (how despawn, the default), walks 15 m away from V first and is removed there (walk_away), or walks off and is removed only once V can't see it and it is at least distance_m from her (dissolve; with walk false it stays where it is until V walks away; no time limit, and despawn removes it at once), and a picked NPC goes back to its own business (leave). Releasing a substitution that is still waiting for the original to leave V's sight cancels it and touches nothing. who all releases everyone. npc.released follows (and npc.dissolved for a dissolve).

- **Command:** `npc.release`, the bridge method `npc.release`
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** Nothing to undo; spawn a new actor if wanted.
- **Refusals:** `npc_unknown`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` (required) | string | matches `^(all\|[ap][0-9]{1,5})$` | The NPC's handle, or all. |
| `how` | string | `despawn`, `walk_away`, `dissolve`, `leave` | despawn (actors, default), walk_away (actors), dissolve (actors) or leave (picked NPCs). |
| `walk` | boolean | `true`, `false` | With dissolve: walk off first (default true). |
| `distance_m` | number | 5 to 30 | With dissolve: removed only this far from V, 5 to 30 m. Default 15. |
| `restore` | boolean | `true`, `false` | A substituted actor only: leave a fresh crowd person (the original record and look) where the actor stood once it is removed, for the game's own crowd to take over; false declines what npc_substitute asked for. Only an explicit release restores: a fight, a handover, the pause, the kill switch and a load leave no one behind. |

### `npc_substitute`

**Replace a crowd person with an XF actor.** Story Engine route (a), substitution: an XF actor with the look of a plain passer-by of the street crowd takes their place, standing where they stood and facing the way they faced, so the engine can run that person on its own routine. The person is chosen by id (from npc_list), by the handle of a picked NPC (who) or by what V is looking at (look_at); the same refusals as npc_pick apply (story characters, companions, vendors, police, children, bosses, anyone in a scene, anyone in combat or hostile, anyone not part of the street crowd, anyone further than 30 m), and community NPCs (community_npc: a regular at a bench, a stall or a doorway; a quest can reserve one without marking it, and the removal can't be undone, so only lane-crowd passers-by are replaced; it is checked before anything is held and again just before the removal, and dry_run reports the community identity for diagnostics only). The bridge reads the person's record, appearance, colour variant, gender, place and heading, picks the closest XF cast (a base-game civilian clone, since a crowd record is a lane walker that would rejoin the crowd and ignore commands) and asks for the original's appearance by name. The swap waits for a moment V cannot see the original (outside her view or behind static geometry): then the original is held still, the actor is requested at its spot, and only when the actor stands there is the original removed (hidden for good and marked for the crowd system to recycle), so V never sees an empty spot; npc.substituted follows with the final look_match. An original that stays in view is waited for up to max_wait_s (30 by default), untouched, then given up on (npc.substitute_failed never_hidden); in_view true swaps at once even in V's sight, to see what she would see. The original is looked at once more just before it is hidden: if V can see it by then the swap waits a few seconds, and rolls back if it stays in sight. A swap that cannot finish (the actor never appears, the removal is refused, V or the original cannot be read, V enters a fight or a scene, the pause, a handover, the kill switch) gives the original back to the crowd and removes the actor; the original is found by its own id wherever it is, being returned is reported only after the game confirms it, and one it cannot find is kept and retried for up to a minute (npc.original_returned or npc.original_unreturned follows). Answers the new actor's handle (a1, a2, ...; it works like any npc_spawn actor: npc_move, npc_say, npc_release dissolve ...), look_match (what matched exactly and what is approximated, with the cast, the record relation and what is not attempted: props, body proportions, voice and colour variants; level and confirmed become final in npc.substituted, once the game reports the appearance the actor really wears), resident (a key the Story Engine can keep: a hash of record, appearance and spawn spot (xfr1-...); the key is ours, not the game's, so a reload or a stream-out loses the actor until the engine brings it back with npc_spawn and the look in respawn; the game's own community pair (xfc1-...) appears only in a dry run, as the identity for later true adoption) and respawn (npc_spawn's parameters for the same look at the same spot and heading). dry_run reads and matches without touching anything. restore true leaves a fresh crowd person where the actor stood when it is released (see npc_release); one that never joins the crowd within seconds is deleted, at most five wait at once, and ownership passes to the game only once it is seen in the crowd. reactions game gives the actor the civilian's own reactions, so it flinches and flees as the crowd does. Counts among the 5 actors. Never saved. Needs Codeware and the -writes package's actor records.

- **Command:** `npc.substitute`, the bridge method `npc.substitute`
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The result's undo releases the actor; before the swap is done that cancels it and gives the original back, afterwards the original cannot be brought back (it was hidden for good).
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_world`](#refusal-not-in-world), [`in_combat`](#refusal-in-combat), [`in_vehicle`](#refusal-in-vehicle), [`in_scene`](#refusal-in-scene), [`not_v`](#refusal-not-v), [`codeware_missing`](#refusal-codeware-missing), `npc_protected`, `npc_busy`, [`npc_not_found`](#refusal-npc-not-found), [`too_far`](#refusal-too-far), `limit`, `look_unmatched`, `community_npc`, `cast_unknown`, `already_substituting`, `record_missing`, [`not_ready`](#refusal-not-ready), [`not_streamed`](#refusal-not-streamed), `not_walkable`, [`spawn_refused`](#refusal-spawn-refused), [`incident_unknown`](#refusal-incident-unknown), [`incident_limit`](#refusal-incident-limit), [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | 1 to 64 characters | The person's id from npc_list. |
| `who` | string | matches `^p[0-9]{1,5}$` | The handle of a picked NPC (p1, ...): the pick is let go once it is replaced. |
| `look_at` | boolean | `true`, `false` | The NPC V is looking at. |
| `cast` | string | `woman_corpo`, `man_corpo`, `woman_nightlife`, `man_youngster`, `woman_lowlife`, `man_lowlife`, `woman_masked`, `man_masked` | Use this civilian cast instead of the closest one. |
| `label` | string | 1 to 40 characters | The name its lines and dialogue choices show (default Stranger). |
| `reactions` | string | `quiet`, `game` | quiet (the default: no crime or panic reactions) or game (an ordinary passer-by's own reactions). |
| `restore` | boolean | `true`, `false` | When the actor is released, leave a fresh crowd person (the original record and look) where it stood. Default false. |
| `in_view` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Swap at once even if V can see the original (to observe the pop). Default false: wait for a moment she cannot. |
| `max_wait_s` | number | 1 to 120 | How long to wait for the original to leave V's sight, 1 to 120 s. Default 30. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Read the person, match the look and report the resident key and respawn parameters; hold nothing, spawn nothing. |
| `incident` | string | 1 to 64 characters | Test build only: the id of a declared incident (incidents_declare) the actor joins, by the handle it is given, as soon as the request is made. Not with dry_run. |
| `incident_role` | string | 1 to 32 characters | With incident: the engine's own role name for the actor (default participant). |

### `npc_scenario`

**Run an NPC scene.** Runs a short NPC scene written as data (tools/npc/scenarios): name picks a bundled one (stranger_question: an XF actor walks up to V, greets her, asks a question, offers two answers and reacts to the one the player picks), or file a scene file. Each step is an npc command or a wait for an event; the player's pick decides the branch. When the scene ends, fails or is stopped, every actor it brought in is released. dry_run checks the scene and lists its steps without touching the game. Answers the steps taken, the events, the player's answer and how long each part took.

- **Command:** `npc.scenario`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Direct NPCs (`write-npc`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** The scene releases every actor it brought in when it ends, fails or is stopped; the kill switch and loading a save do too.
- **Refusals:** `scenario_invalid`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `stranger_question` | A bundled scene. |
| `file` | string | 1 to 400 characters | A scene file (JSON) instead. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Check the scene and list its steps; nothing reaches the game. |

## Capture and the agent's view

Screenshots from outside the game (they work without the bridge), re-crops, bursts and contact sheets, and the scene report: the agent's own view of the shot without a screenshot.

### `capture_screenshot`

**Screenshot the game.** Takes a screenshot of the game window from outside the game (what is on screen, including ReShade and overlays). Optionally keeps only an area (region, rect or rect_normalized). Saves the area at full resolution and returns a smaller copy for viewing (at most 1280 px on the long side unless max_width, max_height or scale says otherwise) plus the path of the full-resolution file.

- **Command:** `capture.screenshot`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** `capture_no_window`, `capture_minimized`, `capture_not_foreground`, `capture_blank`, `capture_failed`, [`expectation_failed`](#refusal-expectation-failed)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | `full`, `center-16x9`, `head-and-shoulders`, `face`, `eyes`, `full-body`, `cc-eyes` | Named area to keep: full (The whole game window.); center-16x9 (The central 16:9 area: on an ultrawide window, the part a 16:9 screen would show.); head-and-shoulders (A centred area around V's head and shoulders in the photo-mode face framing.); face (A centred area around V's face, matching photo.frame's face framing.); eyes (A centred band across both of V's eyes and brows, matching photo.frame's eyes framing.); full-body (A centred full-height area around V standing, matching photo.frame's full-body framing.); cc-eyes (V's eyes and brows in the character creator's eyes zoom (the creator's own camera, not photo mode).). Default: full. |
| `rect` | object | the fields below | Area to keep, in pixels of the game window (instead of region). |
| `rect.x` (required) | integer | 0 to 16384 | Left edge, in pixels of the game window |
| `rect.y` (required) | integer | 0 to 16384 | Top edge, in pixels of the game window |
| `rect.width` (required) | integer | 1 to 16384 | Width, in pixels of the game window |
| `rect.height` (required) | integer | 1 to 16384 | Height, in pixels of the game window |
| `rect_normalized` | object | the fields below | Area to keep, as fractions of the window's width and height from 0 to 1 (instead of region). |
| `rect_normalized.x` (required) | number | 0 to 1 | Left edge, as a fraction of the window (0 to 1) |
| `rect_normalized.y` (required) | number | 0 to 1 | Top edge, as a fraction of the window (0 to 1) |
| `rect_normalized.width` (required) | number | 0 to 1 | Width, as a fraction of the window (0 to 1) |
| `rect_normalized.height` (required) | number | 0 to 1 | Height, as a fraction of the window (0 to 1) |
| `max_width` | integer | 16 to 16384 | Largest width of the returned picture, in pixels. Default: 1280 on the long side. |
| `max_height` | integer | 16 to 16384 | Largest height of the returned picture, in pixels. |
| `scale` | number | 0.01 to 1 | Shrink the returned picture by this factor (0.01 to 1) instead of a size limit. |
| `name` | string | at most 80 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}$` | Short label for the files (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'). |
| `route` | string | `auto`, `printwindow`, `screen` | How to grab the window. auto (default) reads Windows' copy of the game window, then the screen if the game is in front; printwindow and screen force one route. The screen route reads only while the game is the front window (checked right before and after each grab), otherwise it refuses capture_not_foreground. |
| `clear_overlay` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Keep the bridge's own overlay out of the picture: its message lines are cleared and its HUD panel and label hidden for the capture, then the panel comes back (default true; needs the game bridge). |
| `expect` | object | the fields below | Checks judged before the capture from the scene report (subject in frame with a margin, not blocked, lit) and after it on the subject's region (mean luminance, clipped highlights, crushed shadows); on_fail says what a failure does. |
| `expect.subject` | string | at most 80 characters | The subject: v, face, head or body (V), piece:&lt;index> (a showroom head) or an NPC's id. Default V, else the first showroom head. |
| `expect.in_frame_margin` | number | 0 to 0.5 | Wholly in frame with at least this margin to every edge, in window heights (0 to 0.5). |
| `expect.unoccluded` | boolean | `true`, `false` | No static geometry between the camera and the face. |
| `expect.lit_by` | string | `any`, `photo`, `rig` | At least one light reaches the face: any, photo (photo mode's) or rig (the showroom's). |
| `expect.luminance` | array of number | exactly 2 items; each 0 to 1 | The subject region's mean luminance within [low, high] (0 to 1). |
| `expect.max_clipped` | number | 0 to 1 | At most this share of the region clipped (any channel at 250 or more), 0 to 1. |
| `expect.max_crushed` | number | 0 to 1 | At most this share of the region crushed (luminance at 5/255 or less), 0 to 1. |
| `on_fail` | string | `refuse`, `warn` | refuse (default): a failed check before the capture takes none, one after it answers expectation_failed (the file is kept for inspection); warn: capture anyway and list the failures. |
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | A showroom build's folder or manifest.json, so lit_by can judge its rig lights. |

### `scene_read`

**Read the scene (raw).** The bridge's raw reading of what the camera sees: the active camera's place, direction, field of view and aspect, three calibration points through the game's own projection, V (or her photo-mode stand-in), the NPCs within radius of V (nearest first, with a sight-line check from the camera to each face), XF Finish Showroom's heads and rigs, photo mode's three lights (place, direction, sight line to V's face), the time and rain, and the UI (menus, photo mode's menu and cursor, the interaction and dialogue choices the HUD offers). points (up to 32 world points) are projected by the game itself. scene_report turns this into bounds, margins, light shares and checks.

- **Command:** `scene.read`, the bridge method `scene.read`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parts` | array of string | at most 7 items; each `camera`, `v`, `npcs`, `showroom`, `lights`, `world`, `ui` | Which parts (default all): camera, v, npcs, showroom, lights, world, ui. |
| `radius` | number | 0 to 60 | NPCs within this many metres of V, 0 to 60. Default 20. |
| `max_npcs` | integer | 0 to 32 | At most this many NPCs, 0 to 32. Default 8. |
| `occlusion` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Check the sight line from the camera to each face (default true). |
| `points` | array of array of number | at most 32 items; each exactly 3 items | World points to project with the game's own projection. |
| `piece_eyes` | array of number | exactly 3 items | A showroom head's eyes in its own frame (default [0, 0.0497, 1.691], the showroom build's). |
| `npc_detail` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Also give each NPC its character record's details (affiliation, type, rarity, archetype, attitude group, crowd flags) under "character". Off by default; one extra lookup per distinct record. |

### `scene_report`

**Report what the camera sees.** The agent's own view of the shot, to read instead of a screenshot: the camera (place, direction, pitch, field of view, photo mode's exposure, and whether the projection was calibrated by the game); each subject (V, NPCs near her, the showroom's heads) with its screen bounds (window heights from the centre, x right, y down), the fraction in frame, its margins to each edge, whether static geometry blocks the camera's view of its face, its distance, which way it faces (0 = the camera) and, for V in photo mode, her expression and pose; the lights at the focus subject's face (photo mode's lights and the showroom's rig lights: on, place, whether they reach it, an estimated share); with include frame, statistics of the focus subject's region in a fresh screenshot (mean luminance, clipped highlights, crushed shadows); and the world and UI state. warnings lists what looks wrong (a blocked face, a subject cut by the frame).

- **Command:** `scene.report`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_manifest_bad`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include` | array of string | at most 6 items; each `camera`, `subjects`, `lights`, `frame`, `world`, `ui` | What to report (default camera, subjects, lights, world, ui; frame takes a screenshot). |
| `subjects` | array of string | at most 3 items; each `v`, `npcs`, `showroom` | Which subjects (default v, npcs, showroom). |
| `bounds` | string | `face`, `head`, `body` | The box judged for each subject: face (default), head or body. |
| `focus` | string | at most 80 characters | The subject the lights and frame statistics are judged at: v, piece:&lt;index> or an NPC's id (default: the first showroom head, else V). |
| `radius` | number | 0 to 60 | NPCs within this many metres of V, 0 to 60. Default 20. |
| `max_npcs` | integer | 0 to 32 | At most this many NPCs, 0 to 32. Default 8. |
| `manifest` | string | at most 1024 characters | A showroom build's folder or manifest.json, to judge its rig lights. |
| `frame` | object | the fields below | With include frame: which region, and at what size. |
| `frame.subject` | string | at most 80 characters | The subject whose region is measured (default: focus). |
| `frame.max_width` | integer | 160 to 3840 | Measure on a copy this wide, 160 to 3840 px. Default 960. |

### `capture_sheet`

**Make a labelled contact sheet.** Puts named captures side by side in one labelled grid and writes it to disk with a manifest (which file is in which cell): each cell is an earlier capture (path: its .full.png or viewing copy in the capture folder) or, without a path, a screenshot taken now (region, with the XF overlay out of the picture). For comparisons such as finish close-ups or a highlight sweep: sweep takes showroom_rotate's answer as it came, one cell per captured step labelled with its angle. Give cells, sweep or both.

- **Command:** `capture.sheet`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`bad_input`](#refusal-bad-input), `too_many`, `capture_no_window`, `capture_minimized`, `capture_not_foreground`, `capture_blank`, `capture_failed`

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cells` | array of object | 1 to 48 items | The cells, left to right, top to bottom. |
| `cells[].label` (required) | string | 1 to 80 characters | The label under the picture. |

| `sweep.frames[].capture.view` | string | at most 1024 characters | The viewing copy. |
| `sweep.swept` | array of integer | at most 64 items; each 0 to 64 | The heads swept (as showroom_rotate answers). |
| `sweep.from_deg` | number | -360 to 360 | The sweep's first angle. |
| `sweep.to_deg` | number | -360 to 360 | The sweep's last angle. |
| `sweep.steps` | integer | 1 to 1000 | The number of steps. |
| `sweep.returned` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Whether the heads were turned back. |
| `sweep.undo` | object | the fields below | showroom_rotate's undo (ignored here). |

| `sweep.undo.params` | object | the fields below | The undo's parameters. |
