| `sweep.undo.params.turns[].index` | integer | 0 to 64 | A head's index. |
| `sweep.undo.params.turns[].yaw` | number | -720 to 720 | Its yaw. |
| `title` | string | at most 120 characters | A title across the top. |
| `columns` | integer | 1 to 8 | Cells per row, 1 to 8. Default up to 4. |
| `region` | string | `full`, `center-16x9`, `head-and-shoulders`, `face`, `eyes`, `full-body`, `cc-eyes` | For cells taken now: the area to keep (as capture_screenshot). |
| `max_width` | integer | 320 to 8000 | The sheet's width at most, 320 to 8000 px. Default 2400. |
| `name` | string | at most 60 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}$` | Short label for the files (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'). |

### `capture_arm`

**Arm a source-event capture.** Autonomous test recorder required. One tools-process-owned arm, polled through the same command connection. Fires screenshot/burst/recrop on future exact recorder data.event or session kind (line.widget_created, toast.created, npc.arrived, dm.quest with match). Match uses scalar equality on event data. Delay is measured from source time, with latency bounds recorded; the recorder's identity and activity are checked again just before the capture, and the arm is cancelled if the recorder stopped or restarted. Coverage depends on the trigger's feed: with channel (a recorder event such as line.widget_created on subtitles) the arm is cancelled, with the exact reason, by recorder loss after arming (dropped rows, a writer error, lost history, invalid samples on that channel, missed deadlines on a polled channel: v, actors, camera, ui); without channel it is a session-feed arm (dm.quest, npc.arrived, supervisor.*), cancelled only by session-feed loss, and recorder loss while armed is reported with its receipt (recorder_loss_while_armed). Busy commands/polling can make a capture late. Default keeps overlays for consumer evidence. Count &lt;=8 and expiry &lt;=120s; close/kill/handover cancels. Use a persistent MCP/session runner; a one-shot CLI closes and cancels its arm. Recrop processes an existing image and cannot observe a new event.

- **Command:** `capture.arm`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` (required) | integer | 1 to 9007199254740991 | Recorder run |
| `event` (required) | string | 1 to 64 characters | Exact event name |
| `channel` | string | `v`, `actors`, `camera`, `subtitles`, `voice`, `face`, `ui`, `contacts`, `incidents` | The recorder channel that carries the event; omit for a session-feed event |
| `match` | object | the fields below | At most eight exact event-data fields to match |
| `match.who` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact who |
| `match.actor` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact actor |
| `match.style` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact style |
| `match.quest` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact quest |
| `match.objective` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact objective |
| `match.state` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact state |
| `match.line_id` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact line_id |
| `match.widget_id` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact widget_id |
| `match.speaker` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact speaker |
| `match.text` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact text |
| `match.source` | string | at most 512 characters | Exact source |
| `capture` (required) | string | `screenshot`, `burst`, `recrop` | Capture command |
| `args` | object or object or object | the fields below | Arguments for selected screenshot, burst or recrop; exact command schema checked before arming |
| `delay_ms` | integer | 0 to 2000 | Source-timed delay, default 50 |
| `count` | integer | 1 to 8 | Maximum captures, default 1 |
| `expires_s` | integer | 1 to 120 | Arm lifetime, default 30 seconds |

### `capture_armed`

**Read armed capture receipts.** Current process-owned arm and last 32 receipts, including source event, capture paths and event-to-capture latency bounds. No new capture.

- **Command:** `capture.armed`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)

- **Changes the game:** No

No parameters.

## Saves

List, make and load saves. Only `game_save` ever saves the game, and never over an existing save.

### `game_save`

**Make a manual save.** Makes one new manual save, as the save menu's empty slot does, and waits for the game to confirm it (the game names it ManualSave-&lt;n>; name is only a label for the logs). Never overwrites or deletes a save. Only from normal play. While the bridge's own changes are live it keeps saving locked, and this is refused unless override_lock is true: the save then keeps those changes, and the lock goes back on afterwards. Needs the save permission.

- **Command:** `game.save`, the bridge method `game.save`
- **Permission:** Save and load the game (`write-save`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** None: a save can't be unsaved. Delete it in the game's Load menu if it isn't wanted.
- **Refusals:** [`bridge_save_lock`](#refusal-bridge-save-lock), [`bridge_effects_active`](#refusal-bridge-effects-active), [`saving_locked`](#refusal-saving-locked), [`no_free_slot`](#refusal-no-free-slot), [`save_failed`](#refusal-save-failed), [`save_uncertain`](#refusal-save-uncertain), [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`save_in_progress`](#refusal-save-in-progress)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | at most 64 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{1,64}$` | A label for the logs (letters, digits, spaces, '.', '_', '-'). |
| `override_lock` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Save even though the bridge's changes are live (they are kept in the save). Default false. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | 2000 to 60000 | How long to wait for the game to confirm the save, in milliseconds (default 20000). |

### `game_load`

**Load a save.** Loads the most recent save of this playthrough (latest: true, the game's quick load) or one save by its name in the game's list (for example ManualSave-12); an unknown name is refused with some of the names the game lists. From normal play or the pause menu, and from the main menu (0.8: the menu's own paths, so the player only has to launch the game: latest is its Continue, a name its Load menu's, both through the modded-save path for a save made with mods). Everything since that save is discarded, unsaved progress and the bridge's save lock with it, and the game doesn't ask first, so discard_unsaved: true is required. Not from photo mode or the appearance screen. Then (0.8.2) it waits up to continue_wait_s (default 75) for the load to end and answers as soon as the game is in normal play or reaches its timeout. Puppet attachment cannot identify a press-any-key prompt; the autonomous detector reports fresh UI observations with generation/age and readiness signals, or unknown when unavailable. Start-screen presence is distinct from GSM acceptance, which remains unknown. The bridge never sends a key. continue_wait_s 0 only starts the load (then game_wait). Needs the save permission.

- **Command:** `game.load`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Save and load the game (`write-save`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** None: loading discards everything since that save.
- **Refusals:** [`not_in_gameplay`](#refusal-not-in-gameplay), [`save_not_found`](#refusal-save-not-found), [`metadata_pending`](#refusal-metadata-pending), [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`timeout`](#refusal-timeout)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latest` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: load the most recent save of this playthrough. |
| `name` | string | at most 64 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9 ._-]{1,64}$` | A save's name as the game lists it (for example ManualSave-12). |
| `discard_unsaved` (required) | boolean | `true`, `false` | Must be true: everything since that save, unsaved progress included, is discarded. |
| `continue_wait_s` | integer | 0 to 85 | How long to wait for the load to end (gameplay, or the press-any-key screen), 0 to 85 seconds. Default 75; 0 only starts the load. |

### `game_saves`

**List the saves.** The game's save list with each save's details as the Load menu shows them: its name, type (manual, auto, quick, point of no return), location, tracked quest, level, life path, time, play time, game version and whether it was made with mods, newest first (limit, default 20), from normal play, the pause menu or the main menu. The details of the newest limit saves are asked for the way the Load menu asks (each save's screenshot request), and the game sends them a moment after the list; wait_ms (default 3000) waits for them. Loads nothing.

- **Command:** `game.saves`, the bridge method `game.saves`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`unavailable`](#refusal-unavailable), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 200 | How many saves' details, 1 to 200. Default 20. |
| `wait_ms` | integer | 500 to 10000 | How long to wait for the details, 500 to 10000 ms. Default 3000. |

## Overlay and in-game UI

Read the game's UI state and the XF overlay host, and place the bridge's own in-game panel.

### `ui_hud`

**Show, hide or move the ink panel in the game.** Temporary test feature (bridge 0.5.3). The ink panel is drawn in the game's own HUD (ink, in the game's font and colours on the game's own dark plate; it needs Codeware, not Cyber Engine Tweaks): the bridge's connection state and the messages ui.message shows. show hides or shows it; anchor (top_left, top_center, top_right, center_left, center, center_right, bottom_left, bottom_center, bottom_right) with x and y (distance inwards from that corner or edge of the visible screen, in the HUD layer's units: its 3840-wide canvas spans the screen's width from the top-left corner, so on 21:9 the screen shows its top 1600 units, on 32:9 its top 1080; for center, x and y move it from the middle) places it, at least far enough in to keep clear of the game's own HUD blocks (0.8.3: the minimap and quest tracker at the top right, so top_right, center_right and bottom_right sit left of them; the status bars at the top left; the status and cyberware icons at the bottom left; subtitles and prompts at the bottom), and it is kept whole on screen; the default is top_left, 40, 360, under the status bars. scale sizes it (0.5 to 2.5). layer chooses where it draws: photo_menu (default, 0.8.6: the HUD in play and, while photo mode is open, inside photo mode's own menu, where it fades with the menu for the hide-UI key, photo_hud_hide and screenshots, and its answers can also be clicked; there the anchors have no HUD floors, and 0.8.7 keeps the panel out of photo mode's own menu, top bar and hint strips, measured from photo mode's widgets), hud (the HUD only, hidden wherever the game hides it: menus, photo mode, the appearance screen, so the XF box shows in photo mode), notifications or top (research). modal (0.8.7) makes the panel inside photo mode's menu hold photo mode's exit while photo mode is open (Esc and the exit hint do nothing); photo mode's camera keys are read natively and can't be held from a contained route, so they keep moving the camera (0.8.6's ModalPopup context held neither, session 14); it takes effect only there, and the kill switch drops it. The panel in photo mode reports to session_log as ink_tree (photo mode's menu root and the XF layer: on each open, and once laid out with the root's width and rectangles), ink_pointer (hover taken, refused while a mouse button is held, replayed, left; presses with their route and actions, answer clicks and ignored releases with the pointer's position) and ink_input (the camera's mouse taken and released; photo mode's exit held by modal). Its laid-out ink_tree event also gives photo mode's zones and the panel's rectangle. nameplates switches XF Finish Showroom's pedestal name labels; cet_label switches the CET line (Cyber Engine Tweaks' one line with a coloured dot at the far top left, the fallback status surface). With no values it only reads the settings; reset: true goes back to the bridge's configured settings. Changes nothing in the game itself.

- **Command:** `ui.hud`, the bridge method `ui.hud`
- **Permission:** Show messages in the game (`notify`)
- **Changes the game:** No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel
- **Undo:** the result's undo: ui.hud with the earlier settings.

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true shows the panel, false hides it. |
| `anchor` | string | `top_left`, `top_center`, `top_right`, `center_left`, `center`, `center_right`, `bottom_left`, `bottom_center`, `bottom_right` | The visible screen's corner, edge or middle the panel sits against. Default top_left. |
| `x` | number | -4000 to 4000 | Horizontal distance inwards from the anchor's edge (from the middle for center), in the HUD's design units, 3840 across a 16:9 screen (-4000 to 4000). Default 40. |
| `y` | number | -4000 to 4000 | Vertical distance inwards from the anchor's edge (from the middle for center), in the same units. Default 360. |
| `scale` | number | 0.5 to 2.5 | Size, 0.5 to 2.5. Default 1. |
| `layer` | string | `photo_menu`, `hud`, `notifications`, `top` | Where the panel draws: photo_menu (default: the HUD in play, inside photo mode's menu while it is open), hud (the HUD only; the XF box in photo mode), notifications or top (research). |
| `nameplates` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Show each XF Finish Showroom head's preset name on its pedestal. |
| `cet_label` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Show the CET line (Cyber Engine Tweaks' status line with a coloured dot, far top left) and its message lines. |
| `modal` | boolean | `true`, `false` | While the panel is inside photo mode's menu, hold photo mode's exit (Esc does nothing); photo mode's camera keys can't be held and keep working (0.8.7, session 14). false lets it go; the kill switch drops it. |
| `reset` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Go back to the configured settings (alone). |

### `ui_state`

**Read what the game's UI shows.** What is on screen besides the world: the game's phase, a menu or popup, the appearance screen, photo mode and whether the bridge hid its menu or the cursor, the gameplay tier, the HUD's interaction prompt and dialogue choices, whether Cyber Engine Tweaks' overlay is open (its windows would be in a capture), the ink panel, the status surface showing, the XF pins and what drew each, the question waiting for the player's answer, and the XF overlay host's state. Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `ui.state`, the bridge method `ui.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

No parameters.

### `overlay_state`

**Read the XF overlay's state.** The XF overlay host (a test feature: XF's own panel drawn over the game, one diagnostic panel, no input yet): whether it is on in this build, hooked, drawing or why not (HDR, the back buffer's format, a missing engine address), the back buffer, the theme (dark or light, from the XF Studio's own colours), frames drawn and its CPU time per frame, whether it is hidden for a capture or yielding to Cyber Engine Tweaks' overlay, which frame-generation modules the game has loaded, and (0.8.22) the motion in force: the live dot's pulse and the settle on a change of state run or stand still (motion: effective full or reduced, with the [overlay] motion setting, Windows' animation-effects setting and the reason). Changes nothing.

- **Command:** `overlay.state`, the bridge method `overlay.state`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo

No parameters.

### `overlay_set`

**Set the XF overlay's look live.** 0.8.22: applies the bridge's [overlay] settings without a restart, in memory (config.ini is not rewritten; a restart goes back to it): theme (dark or light: the XF box restyles before its next frame, the CET window and line take it with their next info refresh, about 2 s; the ink panel uses the game's own colours), motion (auto, reduced or full), diagnostics (the XF box's diagnostics card) and enabled (drawing on or off). enabled works live only when the overlay was on at load; switching on one that was off at load is refused with needs_restart, because its hooks attach only at load. Give at least one. The answer has the values now (with the effective motion), the earlier ones and an undo that puts back exactly the keys given; overlay_state and bridge_info show the values in force.

- **Command:** `overlay.set`, the bridge method `overlay.set`
- **Permission:** Show messages in the game (`notify`)
- **Changes the game:** No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel
- **Undo:** The result's undo (overlay_set with the earlier values); a restart goes back to config.ini.
- **Refusals:** [`needs_restart`](#refusal-needs-restart), [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | `dark`, `light` | The theme. |
| `motion` | string | `auto`, `reduced`, `full` | The motion setting. |
| `diagnostics` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Show the XF box's diagnostics card. |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Draw the XF box (live only if the overlay was on at load). |
| `diagnostics_cpu_ms` | number or null | 0 to 100 | Test builds only (test hooks): a figure in ms both diagnostics bars draw instead of the measured CPU time, to show the warning and danger tones; null clears it. |

## Other tools

Tools not yet sorted into an area above.

### `test_save_delay`

**Hold the next save (test hook).** Test hook for the session checks, only in the -writes package for the dedicated test profile (config.ini's [bridge] allow_test_hooks; elsewhere refused test_hooks_off): the next game_save, once, waits ms milliseconds right after its prepare step (where it has checked the moment and, with override_lock, released the bridge's save lock), checking the kill switch every 50 ms, so a bridge_kill sent meanwhile lands inside the save and nothing is saved. ms 0 disarms. Changes nothing in the game. Needs the save permission.

- **Command:** `test.save.delay`, the bridge method `test.save.delay`
- **Permission:** Save and load the game (`write-save`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** test.save.delay with the previous ms (the result's undo); the hold is used up by the next save anyway.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` (required) | integer | 0 to 10000 | How long to hold the next save, in milliseconds (0 to 10000; 0 disarms). |

### `test_events`

**Read the event probes' records (test probe).** Test probe, only in the -writes package for the dedicated test profile (config.ini's [bridge] allow_test_hooks; elsewhere refused test_hooks_off). Reads the records of the game-events and save-identity probes from their own ring (512 records, at most 20 a second per kind; what goes over is counted in dropped and in the kind's next record), apart from the session's events: kinds session (each lifecycle point of a load or save, with restored, pre_game and the probe's test facts), death, defeated, knockdown, combat, heat (wanted_level, wanted_chase_active), zone (CityAreaType), district (the innermost district's enum name, previous, new_location_discovered), interior (a 2 Hz poll's flips), vehicle (mount and unmount with the seat), vehicle.stolen, vehicle.acquired, journal (hash, class, change type, state; no text), dialogue.hub (hub ids, states and choice counts; no text), dialogue.index (only when the highlight or hub changes), call (contact, phase; only a change), time (a jump of the clock, or the menu's skip), status.count and stim.count (the noisy hooks, counted every 5 s). Every record carries game_s and sim_s; death and defeated also carry the victim's attitude towards V. since reads on from a cursor (next); kinds keeps only those kinds. stims: true switches on the stim tap (row 16), false off. Changes nothing in the game.

- **Command:** `test.events`, the bridge method `test.events`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** stims: false switches the stim tap off again; reading changes nothing.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | integer | at least 0 | Read records from this sequence number on (the last answer's next); 0 or none from the oldest. |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 500 | At most this many records (1 to 500, default 200). |
| `stims` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true switches the stim tap on (allow-listed stims counted every 5 s), false off. |
| `kinds` | array of string | 1 to 32 items; each 1 to 40 characters; matches `^[a-z0-9_.:/]+$` | Only these kinds (a family such as dialogue takes dialogue.hub and dialogue.index); next still moves past the rest. |

### `test_save_identity`

**Write or read the save-identity test facts (test probe).** Test probe, only in the -writes package for the dedicated test profile (config.ini's [bridge] allow_test_hooks; elsewhere refused test_hooks_off). mode write sets the probe's test facts, all named xfs_probe_* so they can never be taken for the real save key: a and b (xfs_probe_a, xfs_probe_b), and pin {c0, c1, b, n} (xfs_probe_sk_c0, _c1, _b, _n, with the check xfs_probe_sk_k worked out by the plugin and written last), or pin "clear" to set them all to 0; arm_before_save: true makes Codeware's Session/BeforeSave write a fresh xfs_probe_b before every save (save-identity row 4), false stops it; persist {value, kib} fills the probe's persistent system (rows 11 and 12; kib 0 to 4096). mode read answers the facts, whether the pin's check holds, and the persistent system (present false once its file is removed from the staged mod). The facts go into any save made after; they are test facts and harmless. Takes no save lock. Needs the save permission.

- **Command:** `test.save.identity`, the bridge method `test.save.identity`
- **Permission:** Save and load the game (`write-save`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** pin "clear" sets every test fact back to 0; arm_before_save: false stops the BeforeSave write.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`game_not_ready`](#refusal-game-not-ready)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `write`, `read` | write or read (default read). |
| `a` | integer | 0 to 2147483647 | xfs_probe_a's value (0 to 2147483647). |
| `b` | integer | 0 to 2147483647 | xfs_probe_b's value (0 to 2147483647). |
| `pin` | object or string | the fields below; or `clear` | The pin {c0, c1, b, n} (each 0 to 2147483647), or "clear". |
| `arm_before_save` | boolean | `true`, `false` | true: Session/BeforeSave writes a fresh xfs_probe_b before each save; false stops it. |
| `persist` | object | the fields below | Fills the probe's persistent system: {value, kib}. |
| `persist.value` | integer | 0 to 2147483647 | The persistent field's value. |
| `persist.kib` | integer | 0 to 4096 | The persistent array's size in KiB (0 to 4096). |

### `test_companion_probe`

**Run the companion probe (test probe).** Test probe, only in the -writes package for the dedicated test profile (config.ini's [bridge] allow_test_hooks, and the package's xfb_companion_probe.exe; elsewhere refused). Launches the bundled companion from the plugin's own folder the way companion@1 will: opened against writers and hashed (sha256), created suspended with no window in a job named at creation (route atomic; assigned if the system refused that, with the reason), the job kill-on-close with one process, a memory cap (memory_mb, default 64) and UI limits, its only inherited handle the pipe for its output, checked in the job before it resumes (else ended), a fixed command line, no shell. mode probe (default): the plugin lists the game's archive/pc/mod folder as the game sees it and asks the companion about its first archive and that folder; the answer has the companion's report (in_job, kill_on_close, active_process_limit, memory_limit_mb, file_seen, folder_archives), plugin_view, and vfs_reaches_child (true when the companion sees what the game sees: MO2's virtual files reach a child of the game). mode sleep starts one that waits seconds (default 600) and keeps its job, so quitting the game should end it (kill-on-close); mode stop ends it now. Changes nothing in the game.

- **Command:** `test.companion.probe`, the bridge method `test.companion.probe`
- **Permission:** Change the world (`write-world`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** mode stop ends a sleeping companion; quitting the game ends it too.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`not_in_this_package`](#refusal-not-in-this-package), [`companion_running`](#refusal-companion-running), [`failed`](#refusal-failed)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `probe`, `sleep`, `stop` | probe (default), sleep or stop. |
| `seconds` | integer | 1 to 3600 | sleep only: how long it waits, 1 to 3600 (default 600). |
| `memory_mb` | integer | 16 to 1024 | The job's memory cap in MB, 16 to 1024 (default 64). |

### `game_continue`

**Press past the press-any-key screen.** Refuses no_safe_route. Start and UI_Skip consumers are located, but their event ABI, executing thread and current-owner lifetime remain uncommissioned. The autonomous game.lifecycle.probe records a read-only plan against the observed prompt generation; it never invokes a consumer or readiness callback. No game.quit is implemented; shutdown/save-flush ordering remains unresolved. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

### `cet_panel`

**Drive the CET window's own controls.** 0.8.22: the XF Runtime Bridge window in Cyber Engine Tweaks' overlay, as the player would use it. diagnostics_open opens or closes its DIAGNOSTICS header, in every build: once, right before the header is drawn (the player's own clicks rule after it); with CET's overlay closed it waits for the next time the window draws, and it is sent again until a draw applies it (a CET reload included). press runs the Pause changes or Resume changes button's own action, exactly as a click would, overlay open or closed: test builds only (the autonomous test hooks and allow_test_hooks, else test_hooks_off), and a Resume never undoes a pause the player set with the button (paused_by_player). A press runs once, after the CET layer claims it; a kill, the client going or a new client cancels it first. Notify class, so it works while changes are paused. bridge_info's cet_panel says what the window last drew (diagnostics_open, chip, tone, surface), the recent requests with their status, and how the last press went (last_press). The undo is cet_panel {undo: id}: it puts back what the CET layer captured when it applied that request (the header as drawn before it; the pause state before the press); a header state the window never drew stays unknown, and the header is then left as it is.

- **Command:** `cet.panel`, the bridge method `cet.panel`
- **Permission:** Show messages in the game (`notify`)
- **Changes the game:** No: it shows or moves the bridge's own messages and panel
- **Undo:** The result's undo (cet_panel {undo: id}): the header as it was drawn before, and the pause state before the press.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`paused_by_player`](#refusal-paused-by-player), [`writes_disabled`](#refusal-writes-disabled), [`cet_not_answering`](#refusal-cet-not-answering)

| `undo` | integer | 1 to 9007199254740991 | Put back what that request (its id) changed; takes no other option. |

### `supervisor_set`

**Supervise an actor.** Autonomous test build and allow_test_hooks only. Arms one entry of the supervisor: for V or (0.8.19) for an XF actor, at 3 Hz by default. Up to 5 entries are held at once (V plus four actors, or five actors); setting an actor again replaces only that actor's entry. An actor's entry takes hold_position (the observer detects departures from its radius; it never moves the actor itself) or idle_safe, the invariants alive, not_in_combat and not_lost (the actor still exists and is streamed in), and the policies release (npc.release, despawn), return_last_safe (npc.place to its observed quiet point, within 30 m of V as npc.place requires), pause_world and handover; only XF actors from npc_spawn or npc_substitute (a1, a2, ...) can be supervised, never picked passers-by. An actor's entry is cancelled by the kill switch, a handover, the pause and a load, like V's, and ends by itself when the actor is lost (unless not_lost selects a policy). Admission follows the actor: V's entry needs the player permission, an XF actor's entry the NPC permission (and not the player one), each plus the capability of every policy it selects. Observes a hold-position goal (including optional facing within 15 degrees) or idle safety, then applies the selected fixed policy on a violation edge. No walking or movement hold is implied. Last safe means a stationary quiet interval under partial contact coverage; traffic risk stays unknown. Unknown road classification causes a note only. Player input, kill, handover, pause, load or owner disconnect cancels it. Spawned-object references are a reserved adapter and are refused. Arming requires every selected policy capability: world for pause, both NPC and DM for withdrawal, NPC for an actor's release and return, and control for handover (and, for V, stop and return) alongside the entry's own permission. Each native action retains the arming caller grant and also obeys config; nearby withdrawal removes only our spawned NPCs, props and vehicles still within 30 m, never adopted passers-by. Return first releases our holds then uses the last observed quiet point through the normal teleport checks; missing evidence or combat refuses it. Start recording with the supervisor channel to retain interventions, or read the session events. Optional when compares live conditions immediately before each native changing frame; unmet conditions return precondition_failed with observed state. Autonomous test candidate only. Multi-step actions can refuse after earlier steps; external key routes cannot provide this guarantee.

- **Command:** `supervisor.set`, the bridge method `supervisor.set`
- **Permission:** Move V (`write-player`)
- **Changes the game:** Yes
- **Undo:** supervisor.clear cancels the entry and queued actions. Actions already performed keep their ordinary command undo.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`actor_unavailable`](#refusal-actor-unavailable), [`supervisor_unavailable`](#refusal-supervisor-unavailable), `interrupted`, [`permission_denied`](#refusal-permission-denied), [`supervisor_limit`](#refusal-supervisor-limit), [`precondition_failed`](#refusal-precondition-failed), [`precondition_unavailable`](#refusal-precondition-unavailable)

### `incidents_list`

**What V witnessed.** Autonomous -writes test build and allow_test_hooks only. Read only, passive: nothing here, and nothing in the taps behind it, changes the game or anyone's ties or beliefs. The recent incidents (a theft, an assault, an accident, a street fight, a police stop, gunfire, or other) that the game's own producing systems raised near V, grouped from stimulus broadcasts (gunshots, explosions, blows, crime witnessed, vehicle collisions, screams), deaths and defeats, combat targets, the game's reprimands, vehicle thefts and combat or fear barks, newest first. Each carries a stable id (inc-N), its kind and what it was judged from, the people in it (entity, record, affiliation, roles, an XF actor's handle when it is one, V among them when V took part), where (the middle, first and last place, and V's district) and when (simulation and game seconds), and how V perceived it: saw (a person other than V was inside the camera's view, within 80 m, with no static geometry on the ray from the camera) and heard (V was inside the stimulus' own audible radius), each with its count and nearest distance, and was told, which is not sensed and is never reported. An incident is witnessed when V saw or heard any of it; one that closes witnessed with enough evidence (one shot, blow or death; four barks) becomes one witness.report in test.events, session.events and the recorder's incidents channel, with a confidence from the modes and the evidence. v_involved says V took part. Bounded: 32 open incidents, 64 kept, 24 observations built a second (12 of them weak kinds, 2 of one kind from one entity, every refusal counted in stats as tap_dropped_cap, tap_dropped_weak and tap_dropped_repeat), 40 accepted a second, 20 reports a minute; a report over the minute waits in a queue of 64 (pending_reports) and goes out, marked delayed, as the allowance recovers; if the queue is full too a witness.gap event names the incident (report_gaps). An incident that has run 120 s is closed and continued even with nothing new happening. tap false switches the observation tap off (closing, and reporting, what is open), true on (default on). Sampled when the game raised each event, not continuously. retained_gaps (0.8.21) lists the last 64 witness.gap events, so a report lost to a full queue, or still waiting when a kill, a shutdown or an unload ended delivery (reason transport_down), is found at the next read; a report waiting for the allowance is delivered by the plugin's own per-tick housekeeping, with or without the taps, and at once when the taps go off.

- **Command:** `incidents.list`, the bridge method `incidents.list`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** tap: true switches the taps back on; reading changes nothing.
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string | `open`, `closed`, `any` | open, closed or any (default). |
| `witnessed` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Only incidents V did (true) or did not (false) perceive. |
| `v_involved` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Only incidents V took part in (true) or watched from outside (false). |
| `declared` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Only the engine's declared incidents (true) or only the game's own (false). |
| `id` | string | 1 to 64 characters | Only the incident declared under this id (incidents_declare's id). |
| `limit` | integer | 1 to 64 | At most this many, newest first (1 to 64, default 20). |
| `tap` | boolean | `true`, `false` | false switches the incident taps off (the open incidents are closed and reported first), true on again (default: unchanged). |

### `incidents_declare`

**Declare a staged incident.** Autonomous -writes test build and allow_test_hooks only. Read only towards the game, passive: nothing here, and nothing in the sampler behind it, changes the game or anyone's ties or beliefs. The game raises almost none of the Story Engine's incident kinds (no NPC theft, no stall collection), so the engine stages its own with XF actors and declares them, and V's report carries the engine's own id and kind. id and kind are the engine's own text, kept exactly as given (ASCII letters, digits and _ - . : / +; kind also single spaces; id up to 64 characters, kind up to 48). roles maps XF actor handles (a1, a2, ..., at most five, each one of the bridge's own actors, spawning or out) to the engine's own role names (up to 32 characters); V and picked passers-by (p1, ...) are refused. at is the place, [x, y, z]; without it the middle of the actors' known places. ttl_s is how long it may stay open, 1 to 300 simulation seconds (default 60; a paused game ages nothing). It opens at once and answers our id (inc-N) beside the engine's. While it is open: any stimulus or observation that names one of its actors joins it instead of opening an 'other' (an ordinary incident that shares people with it merges into it and the declared id and kind stay; strangers near it do not join); and the plugin samples V's sight of its actors twice a second, over at most four declared incidents, with the same view cone and static-geometry ray as the taps, so a silent staging can still be seen. Gunshot or shout stimuli near V still give heard. It ends on incidents_close, when the TTL runs out, or with a reason on a kill, a load, a handover or the taps going off; the result is exactly one witness.report that carries declared {id, kind, roles, at, ttl_s} beside the usual fields (kind there is the bridge's own reading of the evidence, usually other; declared.kind is the engine's), a witness.gap if the report queue overflowed, or, if V neither saw nor heard it, one witness.unwitnessed event with the reason (no_samples, actors_missing, no_view, out_of_range, not_in_view, occluded, unchecked). A declared incident is reported whatever its evidence score. Bounds: four declared incidents open, five actors each, an id is not reused while the bridge remembers it (the 64 most recent closed). npc_spawn and npc_substitute take incident (this id) and incident_role so a new actor joins it.

- **Command:** `incidents.declare`, the bridge method `incidents.declare`
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** incidents_close with the same id ends it (a report, or an unwitnessed event, as ever).
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`tap_off`](#refusal-tap-off), [`handed_over`](#refusal-handed-over), [`duplicate_id`](#refusal-duplicate-id), [`incident_limit`](#refusal-incident-limit), [`npc_not_found`](#refusal-npc-not-found), [`no_place`](#refusal-no-place)

| Parameter | Type | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string | 1 to 64 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/+-]+$` | Your own id for the incident, kept exactly: 1 to 64 letters, digits and _ - . : / +. |
| `kind` (required) | string | 1 to 48 characters; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/+-]+( [A-Za-z0-9_.:/+-]+)*$` | Your own name for what happened, kept exactly: 1 to 48 letters, digits, single spaces and _ - . : / +. |
| `roles` | object | any | XF actor handles to role names, e.g. {"a1": "thief", "a2": "mark"}: at most five actors, each role 1 to 32 letters, digits, single spaces and _ - . : / +. Required unless at is given (actors can then join with npc_spawn's incident). |
| `at` | array of number | exactly 3 items | Where it happens, [x, y, z] in world metres. Default: the middle of the actors' known places. |
| `ttl_s` | number | 1 to 300 | How long it may stay open, 1 to 300 simulation seconds. Default 60. |

### `incidents_close`

**Close a declared incident.** Autonomous -writes test build and allow_test_hooks only. Closes the incident declared under id and answers how it ended: outcome report (the witness.report, also in the answer's report), report_queued (witnessed, and the report waits for the minute's allowance), gap (a witness.gap names it) or unwitnessed (V never perceived it; unwitnessed_reason says why). Exactly one of them is also delivered to test.events, session.events and the recorder's incidents channel. Passive. An id that is not open (it closed already: incidents_list with id shows how) is refused.

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string | 1 to 64 characters | The id the incident was declared under. |

### `game_catchup`

**Catch up with the moving session.** Autonomous test recorder required. Read this at the start of each turn: source path/health/combat/heat/vehicle/busy changes, F/U/subtitle/voice callbacks, session events and alerts since a cursor, plus the existing current digest. The page can be behind real time (more: true, with a backlog object of records, events and seconds behind and a summary line saying so): v.current is the newest V only when it comes from the digest (source digest, stale false); with the digest off it is a recorder sample explicitly marked historical and stale, with its age, and a recorder page counts as caught up only when the cursor has reached the latest sequence the recorder showed on the final read. v.latest, v.path and the counts describe only the page read. counts[channel] is every record read for that channel; count_detail[channel] says where they went (invalid ones, polled snapshots coalesced into &lt;channel>_latest, listed events, those omitted from the compact list), so a count and its list reconcile. A cursor's source_counters baseline is checked against the recorder's totals and refused (invalid_cursor) if it could not have been a past reading. First call supplies run; subsequent calls replay cursor verbatim. Compact by default (last 24 events per channel with omitted counts); detail returns all retained records. Loss/invalid sources are explicit and describe the interval since the cursor, not the whole run; contact alerts require explicit receipts, partial car-hit entry and controller report paths are instrumented but uncommissioned, never full no-contact proof. Supervisor summaries reconcile both feeds across calls and include only this recorder run's world and source interval: counts and receipts are what is new since the cursor, already_reported says how many on these feeds an earlier call reported, run_totals and recent carry the run so far (the cursor keeps them), and writes lists the supervisor's own writes and refusals (linked to its actions by cid). Bounded reconciliation compaction is explicit incomplete history. Raw feeds remain available for audit. No second history store.

- **Command:** `game.catchup`, run by the tools (it may call the bridge several times)
- **Permission:** Look (`read`)
- **Changes the game:** No
- **Undo:** nothing to undo
- **Refusals:** [`test_hooks_off`](#refusal-test-hooks-off), [`recording_changed`](#refusal-recording-changed)

| `cursor.supervisor_totals.cancellations` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | The run's supervisor cancellations so far |
| `cursor.supervisor_totals.writes` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | The run's supervisor writes so far |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent` | array of object | at most 8 items | The run's latest supervisor receipts, compact; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent[].receipt_seq` (required) | integer | 1 to 9007199254740991 | Receipt identity |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent[].event` (required) | string | at most 64 characters | Receipt event |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent[].source_s` | number | any | Source time |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent[].actor` (required) | string | at most 80 characters | Actor key |
| `cursor.supervisor_recent[].detail` (required) | string | at most 160 characters | What it said |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes` | array of object | at most 16 items | Session writes not yet paired with a supervisor action; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].seq` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Session event sequence |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].kind` (required) | string | at most 32 characters | write or refused |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].cid` (required) | string | 1 to 128 characters | Correlation id |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].method` | string | at most 64 characters | Method |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].code` | string | at most 64 characters | Result code |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_writes[].source_s` | number | any | Source time |
| `cursor.supervisor_unmatched_actions` | array of string | at most 16 items; each 1 to 128 characters | Supervisor action cids not yet paired with a write; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.supervisor_totals_partial` | boolean | `true`, `false` | The cursor predates run totals, so they miss earlier receipts; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.last_v_seq` | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Recorder sequence of the newest V sample seen; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.last_v_source_s` | number | any | Source time of the newest V sample seen; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.incident_counters` | object | the fields below | The incident counters at the cursor, so incompleteness describes the interval since it; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.incident_counters.dropped` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Observations the plugin refused (rate, invalid) at the cursor |
| `cursor.incident_counters.tap_dropped` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Observations the taps' admission refused (cap, weak kinds) at the cursor |
| `cursor.incident_counters.report_gaps` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Witnessed incidents whose report was lost at the cursor |
| `cursor.source_counters` | object | the fields below | Source loss counts at the cursor, so coverage gaps describe the interval since it; preserve returned value |
| `cursor.source_counters.dropped` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Recorder drops at the cursor |
| `cursor.source_counters.invalid` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Invalid samples at the cursor |
| `cursor.source_counters.missed_deadlines` (required) | integer | 0 to 9007199254740991 | Missed sample deadlines at the cursor |
| `cursor.source_counters.file_error` (required) | boolean | `true`, `false` | Native writer error at the cursor |
| `detail` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Include all retained source records and events |
| `now` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Include current digest, default true; false avoids another game-thread read |
| `replay_files` | boolean | `true`, `false` | Recover older history from the native private chunks, default true; bounded 8 MiB/1024 rows per call, more requests the next page |

## Refusal codes

The shared plain wording each code is answered with (`tools/api/errors.ts`), whichever tool gives it. The bridge's own technical message, when there is one, follows as `detail`.

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| <a id="refusal-access-denied"></a>`access_denied` | Windows refused access to the game bridge. Run the XF tools as the same Windows user as the game. |
| <a id="refusal-activation-expired"></a>`activation_expired` | The test activation expired. Check the current screen before arming a fresh fixture. |
| <a id="refusal-actor-unavailable"></a>`actor_unavailable` | This supervisor supports V and the bridge's own XF actors (a1, a2, ...). Picked passers-by and spawned objects need their own validated actor adapter. |
| <a id="refusal-arms-drawn"></a>`arms_drawn` | V has her arm cyberware out, and the game doesn't swap arm cyberware while it is drawn. Nothing was changed. Holster it first (player_action with weapon.holster), or leave holster_first on so the tools do it. |
| <a id="refusal-bad-input"></a>`bad_input` | A value doesn't fit the tool's input schema (the message lists each problem), or two options that exclude each other were both given. Nothing was sent to the game. |
| <a id="refusal-bad-params"></a>`bad_params` | Some of the values given aren't valid for this action. |
| <a id="refusal-bad-request"></a>`bad_request` | The game bridge didn't understand the request. This is a bug in the tool that sent it. |
| <a id="refusal-bad-version"></a>`bad_version` | The game bridge speaks a different protocol version. Update XF Runtime Bridge and the XF tools together. |
| <a id="refusal-behaviour-limit"></a>`behaviour_limit` | Too many behaviours are running already (at most 4), so this one didn't start. Stop one with behave_stop first. |
| <a id="refusal-bridge-busy"></a>`bridge_busy` | Another XF tool is connected to the game bridge right now. Close it (or wait a few seconds) and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-bridge-effects-active"></a>`bridge_effects_active` | Saving is refused while the bridge holds changes. Release the holders named in detail, then save again. |
| <a id="refusal-bridge-save-lock"></a>`bridge_save_lock` | The bridge has changed the game since the last load, so it keeps saving locked (a save now would keep those changes). Nothing was saved. Load a save first, or ask again with override_lock if the save should keep them. |
| <a id="refusal-busy"></a>`busy` | The game has too many requests waiting. Wait a moment and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-call-failed"></a>`call_failed` | The game refused the call, and nothing is known to have changed. |
| <a id="refusal-carrier-not-loaded"></a>`carrier_not_loaded` | The animation set isn't loaded. For the XF live carrier: install the XF Live Pose test package, open photo mode and select the carrier pose (photo_pose_set with record xfs_live_carrier), then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-carrier-not-selected"></a>`carrier_not_selected` | The XF live carrier isn't the selected photo-mode pose, so nothing was written. Select it with photo_pose_set (record xfs_live_carrier), then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-cet-not-answering"></a>`cet_not_answering` | The XF Runtime Bridge window in Cyber Engine Tweaks hasn't taken the last requests. Check that the game runs with Cyber Engine Tweaks and the bridge's CET mod, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-choice-changed"></a>`choice_changed` | The dialogue offer changed before the requested line was confirmed. Read it again before choosing. |
| <a id="refusal-choice-unsupported"></a>`choice_unsupported` | This dialogue's input and eligibility rules have not been validated. Leave this choice to the player. |
| <a id="refusal-client-timeout"></a>`client_timeout` | The game bridge didn't answer. The game may be frozen or loading; try again shortly. |
| <a id="refusal-clip-not-found"></a>`clip_not_found` | The animation set is loaded but has no clip with that name. Check the name, or the test package's build. |
| <a id="refusal-codeware-missing"></a>`codeware_missing` | The showroom spawns its heads and lights through Codeware, which the game hasn't loaded. Install Codeware 1.20 or newer from its official release page (the bridge never installs it), then restart the game. Nothing was spawned. |
| <a id="refusal-companion-running"></a>`companion_running` | A sleeping companion probe is already running. End it with test_companion_probe {mode: "stop"}, or quit the game, which ends it. |
| <a id="refusal-connect-failed"></a>`connect_failed` | Couldn't connect to the game bridge. Restart the game and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-creator-leave-disabled"></a>`creator_leave_disabled` | Opening, confirming or backing out of the appearance screen is switched off in this bridge's config.ini (allow_creator_leave; only the XF test profile's build allows it). Ask the player to open it, or to press Confirm or Back. |
| <a id="refusal-creator-open-timeout"></a>`creator_open_timeout` | The game was asked to open the appearance screen but didn't within the wait, so the request was withdrawn and the appearance screen won't open (the pause menu may open instead: close it with Esc). Saving stays locked until a save is loaded. Close any menu and try again, or ask the player to open it (a mirror, or F12 with Character Customization Anywhere). |
| <a id="refusal-creator-open-uncertain"></a>`creator_open_uncertain` | The game took the request to open the appearance screen but it hadn't opened by the end of the wait, so it may still open. Check game_status: if the phase is character_menu, use cc_back to close it. Saving stays locked until a save is loaded. |
| <a id="refusal-disconnected"></a>`disconnected` | The connection to the game closed. Is the game still running? |
| <a id="refusal-duplicate-id"></a>`duplicate_id` | That incident id is open already, or the bridge still remembers a closed incident under it. Close the open one (incidents_close) or declare this one under a new id. |
| <a id="refusal-expectation-failed"></a>`expectation_failed` | The pre-capture check failed, so no screenshot was taken. The answer lists which check failed and why; fix the framing or light and try again, or pass on_fail: warn to capture anyway. |
| <a id="refusal-face-table-unreadable"></a>`face_table_unreadable` | Photo mode's expression records couldn't be read, so the bridge can't check which face table index an expression has; nothing was applied. Pass unlisted: true to apply the index anyway (photo_state with options shows face_table). |
| <a id="refusal-failed"></a>`failed` | Something went wrong inside the game bridge. The plugin log has the details. |
| <a id="refusal-game-loading"></a>`game_loading` | The game is loading (or still starting), so the bridge doesn't call into it until the loaded session's player is in; nothing was called or changed. Wait with game_wait for phase gameplay, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-game-not-ready"></a>`game_not_ready` | The game isn't ready for this yet. Load a save and wait until you can move, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-game-not-running"></a>`game_not_running` | The game hasn't finished starting. Wait for the main menu, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-handed-over"></a>`handed_over` | The session is handed over to the player (session_handover), so the bridge changes nothing until session_resume. Nothing was changed. |
| <a id="refusal-in-combat"></a>`in_combat` | V is in combat, so the bridge won't move or act for her now. Nothing was changed. Try again once the fight is over. |
| <a id="refusal-in-scene"></a>`in_scene` | A scene is playing (or V is in a dialogue), where the bridge doesn't move or act for V. Nothing was changed. Wait for the scene to end. |
| <a id="refusal-in-vehicle"></a>`in_vehicle` | V is in a vehicle, so the bridge won't move her or act for her now. Nothing was changed. Get out first. |
| <a id="refusal-incident-limit"></a>`incident_limit` | A declared incident holds at most five actors, and at most four are open at once. Close one with incidents_close first. |
| <a id="refusal-incident-unknown"></a>`incident_unknown` | No declared incident is open under that id (it may have closed already: incidents_list with id shows how). Declare it first with incidents_declare. |
| <a id="refusal-input-busy"></a>`input_busy` | An input test is already pending. Wait for its receipt before starting another. |
| <a id="refusal-input-overlap"></a>`input_overlap` | A real held control overlaps this test. Release it before preparing another pulse. |
| <a id="refusal-input-unavailable"></a>`input_unavailable` | The native input adapter has not been commissioned for this game build. No input was sent. |
| <a id="refusal-killed"></a>`killed` | The game bridge was switched off with its kill switch. In the game, open the Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay and press Reconnect in the XF Runtime Bridge window (test builds), or restart the game. |
| <a id="refusal-layout-unrecognised"></a>`layout_unrecognised` | The clip's keys aren't laid out the way the bridge expects on this game version, so it stopped without writing anything. Keep the answer (its detail lists every mismatch) and stop the live-pose steps. |
| <a id="refusal-live-pose-disabled"></a>`live_pose_disabled` | Writing the live-pose carrier is switched off in this bridge's config.ini (allow_live_pose; only the XF test profile's -writes build allows it). Nothing was changed. |
| <a id="refusal-live-pose-unavailable"></a>`live_pose_unavailable` | The live-pose commands can't run on this game version (an engine address they need is missing from RED4ext's address library), so nothing was read or changed. |
| <a id="refusal-metadata-pending"></a>`metadata_pending` | The game hadn't sent that save's details yet, so nothing was loaded. Try again in a moment. |
| <a id="refusal-needs-restart"></a>`needs_restart` | The XF overlay was off when the game started, and it can only be switched on at start. Set [overlay] enabled = true in the bridge's config.ini and restart the game; after that it switches on and off live. |
| <a id="refusal-no-active-outfit"></a>`no_active_outfit` | V isn't wearing a wardrobe outfit, so what is equipped already shows. Nothing was changed. Use inventory_equip, or wardrobe_equip with set to put an outfit on first. |
| <a id="refusal-no-bridge"></a>`no_bridge` | The game bridge isn't running. Start the game from the XF test profile (with XF Runtime Bridge enabled) and wait for the main menu; the bridge opens its connection when the game starts. When the connection disappears mid-session: The game bridge's connection is gone: the game has probably closed or crashed. Start it again from the XF test profile. |
| <a id="refusal-no-district"></a>`no_district` | The game hasn't told its district system where V is yet. It does so when V crosses an area border, so a moment after a load, or once V moves, it will. |
| <a id="refusal-no-effect"></a>`no_effect` | That would change nothing in the game, so it wasn't sent: V's photo-mode face animation runs on the stand-in (target puppet, the default), not on the head item. Leave target out. |
| <a id="refusal-no-free-slot"></a>`no_free_slot` | The game has no free manual save slot. Nothing was saved. Delete an old manual save in the game's Load menu, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-no-ground"></a>`no_ground` | There is no walkable ground near that point, so V wasn't moved there. Pick a point on the floor (or pass ground: exact at your own risk). |
| <a id="refusal-no-path"></a>`no_path` | The game found no walkable path to that point, so V didn't move. Pick a point on the same floor and within reach. |
| <a id="refusal-no-place"></a>`no_place` | None of those actors has a known place yet (one that is still appearing has none). Give at, or wait for npc.spawned and declare again. |
| <a id="refusal-no-safe-position"></a>`no_safe_position` | The supervisor has no recorded quiet position yet. Let V stand quietly for the configured interval before testing a return. |
| <a id="refusal-no-such-behaviour"></a>`no_such_behaviour` | No behaviour with that id is running. behave_list shows the ones that are. |
| <a id="refusal-no-such-piece"></a>`no_such_piece` | The showroom has no head with that index. showroom_state lists the heads it has. |
| <a id="refusal-not-added-by-bridge"></a>`not_added_by_bridge` | That item wasn't added by the bridge this session, so it stays in V's inventory. Nothing was removed. |
| <a id="refusal-not-equippable"></a>`not_equippable` | The game says V can't equip that cyberware (a requirement isn't met or its slot doesn't take it), so nothing was changed and nothing was added. cyberware_state shows what the slot holds now. |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-character-menu"></a>`not_in_character_menu` | Character options can only be changed while the appearance screen (a mirror, or the ripperdoc's appearance menu) is open. Open it in the game first. |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-gameplay"></a>`not_in_gameplay` | This needs V in the world (or, for the clock, the appearance screen or photo mode): load a save and close any other menus first. |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-inventory"></a>`not_in_inventory` | V doesn't have that item. Nothing was changed. Ask again with add_if_missing to add one to V's inventory first. |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-photo-mode"></a>`not_in_photo_mode` | This only works in photo mode. Open it with photo_open (or ask the player to press the photo mode key), then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-this-package"></a>`not_in_this_package` | This package doesn't carry that test probe. Only the -writes package for the dedicated XF test profile has it (the companion probe's xfb_companion_probe.exe beside the plugin). |
| <a id="refusal-not-in-world"></a>`not_in_world` | The showroom works while V is in the world or in photo mode. Close menus (or leave the appearance screen) and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-not-ready"></a>`not_ready` | The game can't spawn entities yet. Wait until V can move, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-not-safe-now"></a>`not_safe_now` | The game isn't at a safe moment for the appearance screen (combat, a scene, a vehicle, or somewhere photo mode isn't allowed). Nothing was opened. Walk V somewhere quiet and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-not-spawned-yet"></a>`not_spawned_yet` | That head isn't in the world yet (the game spawns them over a few frames). Try again in a moment; showroom_state shows when it is in. |
| <a id="refusal-not-streamed"></a>`not_streamed` | The world around that point isn't loaded yet, so V wasn't moved there (with ground: exact too). Move V closer first, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-not-v"></a>`not_v` | The player isn't V right now (a Johnny section, or someone else the story puts in V's place), so the appearance screen wasn't opened. Try again once V is back. |
| <a id="refusal-npc-not-found"></a>`npc_not_found` | That handle isn't one of the bridge's XF actors (npc_status lists them), and a declared incident names XF actors only, never V or a picked passer-by. |
| <a id="refusal-outfit-managed-elsewhere"></a>`outfit_managed_elsewhere` | V's outfit is managed by a script mod's outfit system (such as EquipmentEx), which replaces the wardrobe's own requests, so this change would do nothing. Nothing was changed. wardrobe_equip with suspend: true takes that outfit off for now (the story's own request) so equipped clothing draws; resume: true puts it back. |
| <a id="refusal-paused-by-player"></a>`paused_by_player` | The player paused changes with the XF Runtime Bridge window's own button, so only the player can resume them there. Ask the player, then try again. |
| <a id="refusal-permission-denied"></a>`permission_denied` | The caller did not allow every capability this policy needs. Grant the required classes explicitly or choose a narrower policy; nothing was started. |
| <a id="refusal-photo-key-needed"></a>`photo_key_needed` | The game offers no way to open the full photo mode from inside. Use photo_open, which presses the photo mode key in the game window, or ask the player to press it; game_wait with phase photo_mode notices when it opens. |
| <a id="refusal-plan-unavailable"></a>`plan_unavailable` | The supervisor could not safely resolve its action targets. Read the action result and current actor state before replacing the entry. |
| <a id="refusal-player-busy"></a>`player_busy` | V is busy (jumping, sliding, falling or landing, swimming, in a workspot, a takedown or grapple, carrying a body, in a menu, or photo mode is open), so the bridge won't move her now. Nothing was changed. Try again once she stands still in normal play; player_state's busy_state says which. |
| <a id="refusal-precondition-failed"></a>`precondition_failed` | The game state changed before this step could act. The detail contains the required and observed state; read catch-up and prepare the next action. |
| <a id="refusal-precondition-unavailable"></a>`precondition_unavailable` | This route cannot compare conditions on the executing game frame. Use the autonomous test candidate's native action route. |
| <a id="refusal-quest-scene"></a>`quest_scene` | A story scene is playing, and the story may hold the weather itself, so the bridge didn't change it. Nothing was changed. Try again once the scene is over. |
| <a id="refusal-rate-limited"></a>`rate_limited` | The game bridge was sent too many requests in a short time, and it was still refusing after the tools waited a few seconds. Nothing was changed by the refused request. Wait a moment and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-recording-busy"></a>`recording_busy` | The recorder is still active or draining. Stop it and finish saving its records before starting another run. |
| <a id="refusal-recording-changed"></a>`recording_changed` | That recording is no longer current. Use the run identifier returned by its start; never join samples from different runs. |
| <a id="refusal-rtti-missing"></a>`rtti_missing` | This game version doesn't have a function the bridge needs for this action, so nothing was changed. The game may have been updated: the bridge needs a rebuild for it. |
| <a id="refusal-rtti-signature"></a>`rtti_signature` | A game function this action uses has changed shape in this game version, so the bridge refused to call it and nothing was changed. The bridge needs updating for this game version. |
| <a id="refusal-save-failed"></a>`save_failed` | The game answered that the save failed. Nothing new was saved. Check free disk space and the game's save folder. |
| <a id="refusal-save-in-progress"></a>`save_in_progress` | Another save is being made right now (game_save, or Save anyway in the XF Runtime Bridge window). Nothing was saved by this request; try again when it has finished. |
| <a id="refusal-save-lock-not-held"></a>`save_lock_not_held` | The appearance screen wasn't opened because the game hasn't confirmed the bridge's save lock yet. Saving stays locked until a save is loaded. Try again in a moment. |
| <a id="refusal-save-not-found"></a>`save_not_found` | No save has that name in the game's list, so nothing was loaded. The detail lists some of the names the game shows. |
| <a id="refusal-save-uncertain"></a>`save_uncertain` | The game took the save request but didn't confirm it in time. Check the game's Load menu before saving again, so no duplicate save is made. |
| <a id="refusal-saving-locked"></a>`saving_locked` | The game doesn't allow saving right now (combat, a scene, or another lock). Nothing was saved. Try again from a quiet moment in normal play. |
| <a id="refusal-script-calls-unavailable"></a>`script_calls_unavailable` | The bridge can't call into this game version (an engine address it needs is missing from RED4ext's address library), so it refuses every game action this session and nothing changed. Update RED4ext, or rebuild the bridge for this game version. |
| <a id="refusal-script-layer-missing"></a>`script_layer_missing` | The bridge's script part isn't loaded (redscript didn't compile it). Check that redscript is installed and look for a script error at game start. |
| <a id="refusal-script-outfit-api-changed"></a>`script_outfit_api_changed` | The installed Equipment-EX doesn't offer the outfit functions the bridge calls (a different version changed them), so the bridge won't drive its outfit; nothing was changed. wardrobe_equip with suspend: true still takes the outfit off (the story's own request); wardrobe_state names the version and what differs. |
| <a id="refusal-session-running"></a>`session_running` | A scripted session is driving the game, so the MCP server stays off the bridge until it finishes or pauses at a question for the player. Screenshots and the kill switch still work. |
| <a id="refusal-showroom-missing"></a>`showroom_missing` | The game doesn't have the XF Finish Showroom build these heads come from. Stage that showroom build in the test profile (the coordinator does this), restart the game, then try again. Nothing was spawned. |
| <a id="refusal-spawn-refused"></a>`spawn_refused` | The game's entity spawner refused the showroom entity, so nothing was spawned. The plugin log has the details. |
| <a id="refusal-stale-context"></a>`stale_context` | The expected game screen or choices changed. Read the current state and prepare a fresh fixture. |
| <a id="refusal-stale-match"></a>`stale_match` | The appearance screen changed between reading the option and applying the value (another row is in use, or the value at that position has another name), so nothing was applied. Try again; it reads the option afresh. |
| <a id="refusal-superseded"></a>`superseded` | An emergency control (bridge_kill or session_handover) came after this command and cancelled it: a command still waiting never ran, and a running one stopped at its next step. Check the game's state, then send it again if it is still wanted. |
| <a id="refusal-supervisor-busy"></a>`supervisor_busy` | The bounded supervisor action queue is full. Read its receipts and clear or replace the entry before trying again. |
| <a id="refusal-supervisor-limit"></a>`supervisor_limit` | The supervisor already holds five entries (V plus four XF actors, or five actors). Clear one with supervisor_clear and its actor before arming another. |
| <a id="refusal-supervisor-unavailable"></a>`supervisor_unavailable` | Supervision needs an observed, living actor (V, with an available input listener, or an XF actor that has appeared) in unpaused gameplay. Read the game state before arming again. |
| <a id="refusal-tap-off"></a>`tap_off` | The incident taps are off, and a declared incident needs them for the clock and for the sight samples. incidents_list with tap true switches them on. |
| <a id="refusal-test-build-required"></a>`test_build_required` | This action needs the separate autonomous test candidate. Stage that candidate in the dedicated test profile. |
| <a id="refusal-test-hooks-off"></a>`test_hooks_off` | Test hooks are off in this build. Only the -writes package for the dedicated XF test profile has them ([bridge] allow_test_hooks in its config.ini). |
| <a id="refusal-test-run-required"></a>`test_run_required` | Arm a bounded test fixture before submitting this input. |
| <a id="refusal-timeout"></a>`timeout` | The game was too busy to answer in time, and nothing was changed. Try again in a moment. |
| <a id="refusal-timeout-after-start"></a>`timeout_after_start` | The game started this action but took too long to confirm it. It may still have happened: check the game (or the plugin log) before repeating it. |
| <a id="refusal-too-far"></a>`too_far` | That place is more than 30 m from V, so nothing was spawned there. Move V closer or spawn nearer (distance_m). |
| <a id="refusal-too-large"></a>`too_large` | The request was too large for the game bridge. |
| <a id="refusal-ui-target-not-drawn"></a>`ui_target_not_drawn` | The target button was not drawn and available. Open the CET window and let its layout settle. |
| <a id="refusal-ui-target-unavailable"></a>`ui_target_unavailable` | Save anyway is not currently offered. Wait for a real save-lock offer in the open CET window. |
| <a id="refusal-unauthorized"></a>`unauthorized` | The game bridge refused the connection key. Restart the game so the bridge writes a fresh session file. |
| <a id="refusal-unavailable"></a>`unavailable` | That part of the game isn't available right now. |
| <a id="refusal-unknown-method"></a>`unknown_method` | The running game bridge doesn't know this action. It may be an older build: stage the current XF Runtime Bridge build. |
| <a id="refusal-unsupported"></a>`unsupported` | This game doesn't offer a safe way to do that yet. |
| <a id="refusal-unverified-index"></a>`unverified_index` | That face table index matches an expression only by its place in the list, which isn't reliable with an expression pack installed, so nothing was applied. Use an index photo_state found by name (table_index_verified), or pass force: true to apply it anyway. |
| <a id="refusal-user-took-over"></a>`user_took_over` | The player took over (their own movement, jump, crouch, sprint, dodge, mouse or stick), so the glide or look stopped and gave V back. Nothing more was changed. Start it again once the player has let go. |
| <a id="refusal-write-class-disabled"></a>`write_class_disabled` | This kind of change is switched off in the bridge's config.ini (allow_write_classes lists the kinds allowed: photo, world, character, inventory, save, showroom, player, act, npc, dm; inventory stays off until the maintainer allows it, and showroom, player, act, npc and dm are listed only by the XF test profile's build). Nothing was changed. |
| <a id="refusal-write-mismatch"></a>`write_mismatch` | The game took a different value than the one asked for (its menu may have changed since photo_state was read), so the bridge put the earlier value back where it knew it. Read photo_state and try again. |
| <a id="refusal-writes-disabled"></a>`writes_disabled` | Changing the game is switched off in this setup. It is allowed only in the dedicated test profile, where the bridge's config.ini has allow_writes = true. |
| <a id="refusal-writes-paused"></a>`writes_paused` | Changes are paused in the game's XF Runtime Bridge window (Cyber Engine Tweaks overlay). Nothing was changed. Resume them there to continue. |
| <a id="refusal-wrong-server"></a>`wrong_server` | Something other than the game is answering on the bridge's connection, so the XF tools refused to talk to it. Restart the game. |

Codes the tools above name that have no shared wording yet; the answer's own message (from the tools) or its `detail` (from the game) explains each in context:

`already_substituting`, `capture_blank`, `capture_failed`, `capture_minimized`, `capture_no_window`, `capture_not_foreground`, `carrier_missing`, `cast_unknown`, `choice_too_long`, `choices_busy`, `community_npc`, `contact_unknown`, `expression_unknown`, `framing_bound`, `gesture_unknown`, `hud_missing`, `interrupted`, `key_unsupported`, `limit`, `line_too_long`, `look_unmatched`, `no_ai`, `no_capture`, `no_hidden_spot`, `no_light_component`, `no_projection`, `no_radio`, `no_response`, `no_safe_route`, `no_showroom`, `no_such_pin`, `no_window`, `not_a_door`, `not_a_vehicle`, `not_an_npc`, `not_found`, `not_ours`, `not_walkable`, `npc_busy`, `npc_dead`, `npc_handed_back`, `npc_lost`, `npc_moving`, `npc_not_spawned`, `npc_protected`, `npc_releasing`, `npc_unknown`, `one_hub_at_a_time`, `phone_blocked`, `photo_not_allowed`, `photo_open_timeout`, `pin_refused`, `question_gone`, `record_missing`, `rig_unsupported`, `scenario_invalid`, `showroom_manifest_bad`, `showroom_manifest_missing`, `showroom_not_staged`, `target_missing`, `target_unknown`, `template_missing`, `too_many`, `too_many_pins`, `trigger_unknown`, `tweakxl_missing`, `use_light_remove`, `wait_timeout`.
